name: Raipur
desc: Capital city with modern amenities and vibrant culture

touristPlaces.name: Mahant Ghasidas Memorial Museum
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of the oldest museums in central India with ancient artifacts and tribal art.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Established in 1875, this is one of the oldest museums in central India. It houses an extensive collection of archaeological artifacts, ancient sculptures, natural history specimens, coins, and manuscripts.

touristPlaces.name: Nandan Van Zoo & Safari
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sprawling 800-acre forest zoo home to tigers, leopards, and exotic birds.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Spread over 800 acres of lush greenery, Nandan Van offers a unique blend of zoo and forest safari.

touristPlaces.name: Vivekananda Sarovar
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Serene urban lake with a 37-foot Swami Vivekananda statue and musical fountain.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of the most iconic landmarks of Raipur with boating and musical fountain.

touristPlaces.name: Purkhouti Muktangan
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Open-air museum celebrating tribal culture and folk traditions.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Cultural complex featuring replica villages, tribal art installations, and live craft demonstrations.

touristPlaces.name: MM Fun City
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Large amusement and water park — perfect for families.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Popular amusement park with water rides, roller coasters, and entertainment shows for all ages.

touristPlaces.name: Champaran Dham
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Birthplace of saint Vallabhacharya — sacred riverside pilgrimage site on Mahanadi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Holy site where Vallabhacharya was born in 1479. A beautiful ghat on the Mahanadi river.

touristPlaces.name: Dudhadhari Math
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient 16th-century monastery with ornate frescoes and sculptures.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of Raipur's oldest religious institutions with a stunning main temple, ancient frescoes, and a museum inside.

touristPlaces.name: Rajiv Gandhi Smriti Van
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beautiful urban forest and garden — ideal for morning walks and picnics.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Large forested garden in the heart of Raipur with well-maintained trails, open-air gyms, and a serene lake.

touristPlaces.name: Science Centre Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Interactive science museum with hands-on exhibits for all ages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Regional Science Centre with interactive exhibits on physics, biology, space science, and technology.

touristPlaces.name: Telibandha Lake
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hidden urban lake — a peaceful retreat from city bustle.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Scenic lake in the heart of Raipur, perfect for evening walks.

touristPlaces.name: Chokhi Dhani Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Rajasthani-themed ethnic village resort with folk performances, cuisine and crafts.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Chokhi Dhani is an authentic Rajasthani village experience on the outskirts of Raipur. It features traditional folk dances, puppet shows, camel rides, authentic Rajasthani thali, henna art, and handicraft stalls — perfect for families and groups.

touristPlaces.name: Ram Mandir VIP Road
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of Raipur's most famous and architecturally beautiful Ram temples on VIP Road.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Ram Mandir on VIP Road is among the most visited temples in Raipur. Built in traditional North Indian temple architecture with ornate white marble and intricate carvings, it draws thousands of devotees daily. The temple is especially spectacular during Ram Navami and Diwali.

touristPlaces.name: City Mall Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of Raipur's premier shopping destinations with top retail brands and food court.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: City Mall is a popular shopping and entertainment hub in Raipur featuring national and international retail brands, a multi-cuisine food court, multiplex cinema, and gaming zones. A great place for an urban outing with family.

touristPlaces.name: Colours Mall Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Vibrant shopping mall with fashion, electronics, dining and entertainment.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Colours Mall is a well-known commercial complex in Raipur offering a curated mix of fashion retail, electronics stores, restaurants, and recreational facilities. Its central location makes it a popular hangout for all age groups.

touristPlaces.name: Ambuja Mall Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Large format mall with hypermarket, retail brands, dining and multiplex.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ambuja Mall is one of Raipur's largest shopping centres featuring a Big Bazaar hypermarket, fashion and lifestyle brands, a multi-screen PVR cinema, and a broad range of restaurants and cafes. Ideal for a full day of shopping and entertainment.

touristPlaces.name: Zora Mall Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Modern shopping and lifestyle mall with premium brands and entertainment.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Zora Mall is a contemporary retail and lifestyle destination in Raipur housing premium fashion brands, beauty outlets, an entertainment zone, and a food court. Popular among the city's young crowd.

touristPlaces.name: Amuse-O-Rama Water Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Exciting water park with thrilling slides, wave pools and adventure rides.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Amuse-O-Rama is Raipur's popular water and amusement park featuring wave pools, multi-level water slides, rain dance, lazy river, and dry rides. A perfect summer escape for families and friend groups.
touristPlaces.bestTime: March to June; October to November

touristPlaces.name: Telibandha Drive (Marine Drive)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Raipur's lakeside promenade — the city's answer to Marine Drive, ideal for evening strolls.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Telibandha Talab waterfront promenade is affectionately called the "Marine Drive of Raipur." A beautifully developed walkway along the lake shore with lighting, gardens, food stalls, and space for jogging and cycling. One of the city's most loved evening spots.

touristPlaces.name: Banjari Mata Mandir
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beloved goddess temple atop a hill — deeply revered by locals throughout Chhattisgarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Banjari Mata Mandir is one of the most popular and revered temples in Raipur, dedicated to Goddess Banjari — a form of Durga. Perched on an elevated spot, the temple draws massive crowds during Navratri and on Tuesdays. The views from the hilltop are excellent.

touristPlaces.name: Quiet Lake Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Serene natural lake on the outskirts — a peaceful escape from the city.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Quiet Lake is a tranquil water body on the periphery of Raipur that serves as a popular spot for picnics, fishing, bird watching, and early morning walks. The surrounding greenery makes it an ideal retreat for nature lovers seeking calm away from the urban bustle.

touristPlaces.name: ISKCON Temple Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Grand ISKCON temple dedicated to Radha-Krishna with beautiful architecture and prasadam.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The ISKCON temple in Raipur is a stunning Vaishnava temple complex dedicated to Sri Radha Madanmohan. Built in traditional temple architecture with white marble interiors, it features a museum, daily aartis, bhajan sessions, and a restaurant serving delicious satvik prasadam. A spiritually uplifting and architecturally beautiful destination.

touristPlaces.name: Naya Raipur Central Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sprawling urban central park in Nava Raipur — one of the largest in central India.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Central Park in Nava Raipur (the new capital city development) is a meticulously planned 80-acre green space featuring walking trails, cycling paths, themed gardens, an amphitheatre, and open lawns. Designed on the lines of Central Park New York, it is one of the most ambitious urban green spaces in central India.

touristPlaces.name: Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Stadium
touristPlaces.shortDesc: World-class international cricket stadium — one of India's largest and most modern.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium in Nava Raipur is a state-of-the-art facility with a capacity of 65,000 spectators. It has hosted IPL matches, international ODIs, and T20s. The stadium's modern design and excellent facilities make it a landmark of Nava Raipur.
touristPlaces.timings: Open on match days; Tours available on non-match days

touristPlaces.name: Maha Maya Temple Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient and deeply revered Shakti temple — one of the oldest in Raipur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Maha Maya Temple is one of the most ancient and important Shakti temples in Raipur, dedicated to Goddess Maha Maya (a powerful form of Durga). The temple has a history of several centuries and is particularly crowded during Navratri when the nine-day festival transforms the entire area into a spiritual celebration.

touristPlaces.name: Hatkeshwar Mahadev Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic Shiva temple on the banks of Kharun river — over 200 years old.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hatkeshwar Mahadev is a historic and deeply revered Shiva temple situated on the banks of the Kharun River in Old Raipur. Believed to be over two centuries old, the temple is particularly significant during Mahashivratri and Shravan month when devotees pour in from across the region for special pujas and abhishek rituals.

touristPlaces.name: Naya Raipur Musical Fountain
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Spectacular evening musical fountain show with light, water and sound synchronisation.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The musical fountain in Naya Raipur (Nava Raipur) is a beautifully choreographed water, light, and sound show that draws large crowds every evening. The fountain jets synchronise with music and coloured lights to create a mesmerising visual experience — one of the best in central India.

touristPlaces.name: Adivasi Sangrahalaya (Tribal Museum)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Fascinating tribal heritage museum showcasing Chhattisgarh's 42 indigenous communities.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Adivasi Sangrahalaya (Tribal Museum) in Raipur is a dedicated museum celebrating the rich cultural heritage of Chhattisgarh's 42 tribal communities. It features life-size displays of traditional dwellings, tribal art, ornaments, musical instruments, weapons, and ceremonial objects. An essential stop to understand the state's indigenous roots before exploring tribal regions.

touristPlaces.name: Pandri Market
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Bustling traditional wholesale and retail market — the heartbeat of Raipur commerce.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Pandri Market is Raipur's most famous and oldest commercial district, serving as the central hub for wholesale and retail trade in the city. It offers everything from fresh vegetables and spices to textiles, electronics, and daily essentials. The market's energy, narrow lanes, and competitive prices make it an authentic urban experience.

touristPlaces.name: Gurudwara Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Serene Sikh Gurudwara offering langar, spiritual peace, and warm community welcome.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Raipur's main Gurudwara is a beautiful Sikh shrine that is open to people of all faiths. The Gurudwara offers free community langar (meals) every day, religious kirtan, and a calm environment for meditation and prayer. Visitors are welcome to participate in the langar and experience the warmth of Sikh hospitality.

touristPlaces.name: Sendh Lake
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beautiful natural lake on the outskirts of Raipur, popular for picnics and bird watching.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sendh Lake is a picturesque water body located near Raipur, offering a serene natural environment away from urban noise. The lake attracts migratory birds in winter, making it a favourite among bird watchers. The surrounding area has scenic walking paths and open spaces perfect for family outings and picnics.

touristPlaces.name: Blue Water Park Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Popular water and amusement park with multiple pools and rides for all ages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Blue Water Park is a fun-filled amusement destination near Raipur featuring water slides, swimming pools, rain dance, and dry rides. With dedicated sections for children and adults, it is a family favourite especially during summer months. The park also has dining facilities and rest areas.
touristPlaces.bestTime: March to June; October to November

touristPlaces.name: Chhattisgarh Vigyan Kendra
touristPlaces.shortDesc: State-of-the-art science centre with interactive galleries, planetarium and 3D shows.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Chhattisgarh Vigyan Kendra (State Science Centre) is Raipur's premier science and technology education facility. It houses interactive science galleries, a digital planetarium, 3D film shows, outdoor science park, and regular workshops for students. An excellent destination for families and students to explore science in a fun and engaging way.

touristPlaces.name: Kaushalya Mata Temple Chandkhuri
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient temple dedicated to Kaushalya — mother of Lord Ram — the only temple of its kind in the world.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Kaushalya Mata Temple at Chandkhuri, located about 25 km from Raipur, is believed to be the only temple in the world dedicated to Kaushalya, the mother of Lord Ram. Chhattisgarh (ancient Dakshina Kosala) is revered as the maternal grandmother's home of Lord Ram. The temple sits on a beautiful island in the middle of a lake and is reached by a causeway, making it architecturally and spiritually unique.

touristPlaces.name: Marine Drive Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic lakeside promenade — Raipur's leisure waterfront with gardens and food stalls.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Marine Drive Raipur refers to the developed lakefront promenade along Telibandha and surrounding lakes. It features beautifully landscaped walking paths, ornamental gardens, food kiosks, and seating areas overlooking the water. A favourite destination for evening walks, cycling, and casual outings for Raipur residents.

touristPlaces.name: Priya Cinema Hall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Raipur's most iconic single-screen cinema — a vintage movie experience.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Priya Cinema is a beloved old-school single-screen theatre in the heart of Raipur, operating for decades. Watching a film here with its large screen, crowded balcony, and classic interval chai is a nostalgic cultural experience that fast fades from modern cities.

touristPlaces.name: Hotel Basera
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Raipur's legendary heritage hotel for over 50 years — a landmark of old-world hospitality.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hotel Basera is one of the most famous hotels in Raipur, known for its old-world charm, warm service, and excellent vegetarian restaurant that has served generations of travellers and families. A landmark on Pandri, it is an institution more than a hotel.

touristPlaces.name: Nukkad Tea Cafe (Samta Colony)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Raipur's most loved socially-inclusive cafe — staffed by differently-abled and transgender youth.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Nukkad Tea Cafe is a landmark Raipur institution since 2013 that combines delicious tea-cafe food with a powerful social mission, employing hearing-impaired, differently-abled, and transgender staff across branches in Raipur and Bhilai. Warm murals, vibrant decor, and a full menu of teas, coffee, snacking dishes and desserts make it a must-visit.

touristPlaces.name: Evara Cafe (Civil Lines)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Pure-vegetarian cafe in Civil Lines with creative dishes, desserts and beverages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Evara Cafe, in Katora Talab, Civil Lines, is one of Raipur’s best pure-vegetarian cafes, known for thoughtfully crafted beverages, mouthwatering starters, desserts and comfort food. Its cosy vibe attracts students and young professionals.

touristPlaces.name: Arang Temple Town
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Chhattisgarh's 'town of temples' — 40 km from Raipur with 11th–12th century Hindu and Jain shrines.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Arang, 36–40 km from Raipur on NH-53, was an ancient capital of the Haihaya Rajputs. It packs an extraordinary cluster of medieval shrines — the Bhand Dewal Jain temple, Bagh Deval Shiva temple, Panchmukhi Mahadev, Panchmukhi Hanuman, Danteshwari, Chandi Maheshwari and Mahamaya temples — several built in the same ornate idiom as Khajuraho. The 1920-protected Mahamaya temple is a survey-of-India monument.

touristPlaces.name: Bhand Dewal Jain Temple (Arang)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Rare 11th-century star-shaped Jain temple with polished black tirthankara idols.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bhand Dewal in Arang is an 11th-century Jain temple in the Bhumija architectural style, built on a unique stellate (star-shaped) plan rising five storeys. Its sanctum holds three large, highly polished black-stone images of the tirthankaras Ajitanatha, Neminatha and Shreyanasanatha, and the plinth is wrapped in exquisite sculpture bands.

touristPlaces.name: Bagh Deval Temple (Arang)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: 11th-century Shiva temple whose ornamentation rivals Khajuraho.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bagh Deval temple of Arang is dedicated to Lord Shiva and shares the ornate sculptural vocabulary of the Khajuraho group of monuments. Built with a shikhara over a sanctum and richly carved exterior walls, it stands as a masterpiece of the Haihaya period.

touristPlaces.name: Navagaon Ancient Brick Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hidden 12th-century brick Shiva temple on a village tank at Navagaon.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: At the edge of a tank in Navagaon village stands a rarely visited brick temple thought to date to the 12th–13th century, with a later 16th–17th century restoration. Built on a raised platform with a pillared mandapa, antarala and garbha griha, it is a peaceful heritage gem away from the tourist trail.

touristPlaces.name: Chitawari Devi Temple (Dhobni)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: 9th–10th century stellate brick temple rediscovered in the 1970s.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Chitawari Devi temple at Dhobni, near Damakheda, is one of Chhattisgarh's finest hidden jewels — a stellate-plan temple in red sandstone with a brick shikhara, built around 700–750 CE. Originally a Shiva shrine later reappropriated for a local goddess, it survives with its sanctum intact amid rich Karnataka-style mouldings.

touristPlaces.name: Dhoomnath Temple (Saragaon)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Kalchuri-era temple 75 km from Raipur, now a living shrine of Dhoomeshwari Devi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Dhoomnath temple at Saragaon, on the Raipur–Ambikapur road, is a Kalchuri-period temple whose walls carry carvings of Chamunda, Narasimha, Hari-Har and mithun figures. Originally a Shiva temple, its sanctum now holds a sindoor-coated idol worshipped as Dhoomeshwari Devi — a living example of evolving local faith.

touristPlaces.name: Kankali Talab
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient temple tank of the Dashnai sages with a Shiva shrine at its centre.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kankali Talab is one of Raipur's most atmospheric old religious sites, built by the Dashnai Sanyasi sect. At the centre of the tank stands a sacred Shiva shrine, while the principal Kankali temple spreads beneath a majestic banyan tree at the water's edge.

touristPlaces.name: Shadani Darbar (Tatibandh)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Grand Sindhi spiritual complex founded by Sant Shadaramji Maharaj.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Shadani Darbar at Tatibandh is a renowned spiritual seat of the Sindhi community in Raipur, established by Sant Shadaramji Maharaj. The campus features highly ornate temple halls covered with carved depictions of deities and saints, musical fountains, and the Dukh Bhanjan Dhuni. It is equally a centre for social service.

touristPlaces.name: Kaivalya Dham Jain Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Exquisite marble Jain tirth on Patan Kumari Road — Sri Adinath Shwetambar Tirth.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kaivalya Dham, also known as Sri Adinath Jain Shwetambar Tirth on Patan Kumari Road, is Raipur's most prominent Jain pilgrimage site. Its gleaming white marble architecture, meditation halls and tranquil atmosphere make it both a revered temple and a peaceful retreat.

touristPlaces.name: Jagannath Temple Raipur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: First Jagannath temple of Chhattisgarh with an annual Rath Yatra.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Jagannath Temple of Raipur was the first of its kind built in Chhattisgarh, following the sacred tradition of Puri. Its well-proportioned temple tower and vibrant Rath Yatra — where thousands pull the decorated chariots — make it a major annual landmark.

touristPlaces.name: Maa Mahankali Mandir (Civil Lines)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Popular Shakti temple near Akashwani Chowk in Civil Lines.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Maa Mahankali Mandir at Akashwani Chowk, Civil Lines, is a beloved goddess temple of inner Raipur, drawing daily devotees and especially large crowds during Navratri. Its central location makes it a convenient and welcoming first stop for visitors.

touristPlaces.name: Radha Krishna Temple (Samta Colony)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Blissful Radha-Krishna shrine in Samta Colony — a local favourite.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Radha Krishna Temple of Samta Colony is a well-loved neighbourhood mandir known for its peaceful ambience, beautiful idols and lively festival celebrations. Easy to reach by auto-rickshaw, it is a welcoming spiritual stop in residential Raipur.

touristPlaces.name: Hanuman Mandir (Tatyapara, GE Road)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Energetic Hanuman temple on GE Road, packed every Saturday evening.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hanuman Mandir at Tatyapara on GE Road is one of Raipur's most active Hanuman shrines, thronged especially on Saturdays. Along the same corridor stands the neighbouring Shiv Temple, forming a compact spiritual stretch in the city.

touristPlaces.name: Budhapara Lake
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic old-city lake near Mahamaya Temple — a heritage waterbody.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Budhapara Lake is one of Raipur's oldest water bodies, resting close to the Mahamaya temple in the old city. Its calm waters and open surroundings make it a traditional evening-walk spot that connects visitors to the city's historic core.

touristPlaces.name: Mahant Ghasidas Museum Gardens
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sprawling lawns around Raipur's historic museum — a quiet green retreat.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The landscaped gardens surrounding the Mahant Ghasidas Memorial Museum in the heart of Raipur offer shaded walks, benches and open lawns around the 1875 heritage building. A calm pocket of greenery amid the busy civil lines.

touristPlaces.name: Surkhi Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A centuries-old brick-and-stone Shiva shrine half-hidden in fields near Raipur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Surkhi temple is a quiet Kalachuri-era ruin where local farmers still stop to pray. Its weathered stone deities and the evening oil lamps lit by villagers preserve a folk continuity untouched by tourism — the hidden culture of the plains lives on here.

touristPlaces.name: Doodhadhari Monastery Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A 300-year-old Rama monastery with murals, gardens and temple rituals.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Doodhadhari Baithak monastery combines a swami ashram with ornate Rama temples. Its festive Ram Navami processions, Raslila evenings and the chanting culture of the Ramanandi order show the devotional culture that shaped Raipur for three centuries.

touristPlaces.name: Patan Devi Temple, Borid
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient goddess shrine in old Patan town with folk traditions intact.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This old Devi temple in Patan stands quietly among homes, its worn Nagara stones and daily folk offerings (flour lamps, vermilion, forest flowers) showing how Shakti worship remained a village practice for centuries.

touristPlaces.name: Kaushalya Dam Backwaters
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Serene backwaters of the Kaushalya dam — a quiet escape for birders.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beyond the temple town of Chandkhuri, the Kaushalya reservoir spreads into quiet coves visited by cormorants, kingfishers and winter ducks. The hidden charm is in the unmarked village lanes that verge on marsh and watermeadow.

touristPlaces.name: Urla Chhattisgarhi Thali
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Authentic Chhattisgarhi thali famous for fara, chila and bamboo-bag arhar dal.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This popular family-run dhaba-style restaurant serves a complete Chhattisgarhi thali: steamed and fried fara, green-pea chila, bafauri, forest-flavoured arhar dal, and sweet khurma. The menu rotates with what the farms around Urla are harvesting.

touristPlaces.name: Jungle Jalebi Stall (Shankar Nagar)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Street stall famous for jungle jalebi (mahua phool) and spicy bada.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This tiny roadside stall is known across Raipur for jungle jalebi made from mahua flower extract — a Chhattisgarh tribal delicacy rarely found in restaurants. Arrive early; the batter is made fresh each dawn.

touristPlaces.name: Kumar Gaurav Chowk Food Street
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Raipur’s liveliest food street — a nightly festival of local snacks.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: After sunset Kumar Gaurav Chowk becomes a moving feast: moong bhajiya, pakauri with green chutney, dosa carts, chaat and the famous cold lassi. It is where Raipur’s families and students’ culture collides every evening.

touristPlaces.name: Cave Hill & Taur Range, Naya Raipur (Awaited Parks)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Viewpoint over the Kesla valley where the Maikal hills disappear into the plains.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The ridge north of the new capital hides a sprawling forest reserve habitat with little-trampled trails, deer and peacocks. Its hidden charm is the untouched geology — sandstone outcrops and seasonal pools far from city noise.

name: Bilaspur
desc: Rice bowl of Chhattisgarh with rich heritage

touristPlaces.name: Ratanpur Fort
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic 11th-century fort — once the ancient capital of the Haihaya dynasty.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ratanpur Fort dates back to the 11th century when it served as the capital of the powerful Haihaya kings.

touristPlaces.name: Achanakmar Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Pristine tiger reserve in the Maikal Hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Spread across 914 sq km, home to tigers, leopards, gaur, and 150+ bird species.

touristPlaces.name: Mahamaya Temple Ratanpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of the most revered Shakti shrines — a Shakti Peetha.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of the 52 Shakti Peethas, drawing thousands during Navratri.

touristPlaces.name: Kanan Pendari Zoo
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of the largest zoos in central India with diverse animal collection.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Houses over 100 species of animals and birds spread over 4.5 sq km of forest area.

touristPlaces.name: Malhaar Archaeological Site
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient city ruins from the Kushana period.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Malhaar was a thriving ancient city. Excavations have revealed terracotta figurines, ancient structures, and artifacts.

touristPlaces.name: Seorinarayan Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient Vishnu temple complex on the Mahanadi — one of the holiest sites in Chhattisgarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Temple at the confluence of three rivers. Ancient temples dating to the 11th century with extraordinary stone carvings.

touristPlaces.name: Laftinganj Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hidden waterfall near Bilaspur — a local secret surrounded by forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Serene waterfall accessible by a short forest trail from the Bilaspur–Ambikapur road.

touristPlaces.name: Shivani Multiplex
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Bilaspur's most popular multiplex cinema for the latest releases.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Shivani Multiplex is the go-to cinema destination in Bilaspur, screening new Hindi, regional, and English blockbusters with comfortable seating and modern sound. Combined with nearby eateries, it makes for a complete evening out in the city.

touristPlaces.name: Kota Dam (Sant Ravidas Sagar)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic dam on the Kota river near Bilaspur — a relaxed local getaway.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Kota Dam, also known as Sant Ravidas Sagar, is a beautiful water reservoir on the outskirts of Bilaspur ringed by open fields and low hills. It is a favourite spot for evening walks, picnics, and angling, with a temple on the dam complex.

touristPlaces.name: Mini Mall Bilaspur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Compact but lively shopping complex in central Bilaspur for fashion and food.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Mini Mall is a popular commercial complex in Bilaspur’s city centre offering clothing stores, mobile shops, branded fast food outlets, and a small food court. It is a convenient one-stop destination for casual shopping and family outings.

touristPlaces.name: University Cafeteria (Guru Ghasidas University)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Iconic campus cafeteria of GGU, Koni — fondly known for its chai and aloo paratha.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The University Cafeteria at Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya, Koni, is a beloved Bilaspur institution among students, offering home-style snacks, aloo paratha, coffee shakes and chai in the peaceful campus atmosphere. A nostalgic slice of university life.

touristPlaces.name: Devrani Jethani Temple (Tala)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Chhattisgarh's oldest temples — 6th-century twin shrines at Tala with the famous Rudra-Shiva colossus.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Devrani Jethani twin temples at Tala (Amerikampa village, 27 km from Bilaspur) rank among the oldest surviving Hindu monuments of Chhattisgarh, dated to the 6th century. The complex, discovered by J.D. Beglar in 1878, yields superb stone carvings; its crowning treasure is the 2.7-metre monolithic Rudra-Shiva statue unearthed in 1988 — an 8.7-foot icon whose anatomy blends animals and human heads, even honoured on a 2009 Indian stamp.

touristPlaces.name: Lakhani Devi Temple (Ratanpur)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient hilltop goddess temple overlooking Ratanpur — 800 years old.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Perched on the slopes of the sacred Varaha Parvat (also called Lakshmidham or Sri Parvat) at Ratanpur, the Lakhani Devi Temple venerates goddess Lakshmi and is roughly 800 years old. The climb rewards visitors with both darshan and sweeping views over the historic Kalachuri capital.

touristPlaces.name: Pataleshwar Kedar Temple (Malhar)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Classical rock-cut Shiva temple at the Malhar archaeological site.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Pataleshwar Kedar Temple at Malhar, built by the Kalachuri dynasty, is a superb example of classical temple architecture with a sanctum housing a revered Shiva lingam. Its walls are covered with sculptures of deities and mythological scenes reflecting the artistic pinnacle of ancient Dakshina Kosala.

touristPlaces.name: Didneshwari Temple (Malhar)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ornate Durga temple of the Kalachuri period at Malhar.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Adjacent to Pataleshwar Kedar stand the ruins and restored fabric of the Didneshwari Temple, dedicated to Goddess Durga. Intricate carvings, a prominent shikhara and richly detailed columns make it a highlight of the Malhar temple cluster.

touristPlaces.name: Shiv Temple Kirari Godhi
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hidden Kalchuri-era Shiva temple at Kirari Gordhi near Bilaspur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beside a small stream in Kirari Godhi village, 30 km from Bilaspur, stands this 11th-century Kalchuri Shiva temple. Only part of its wall survives, but that wall glows with superb carvings of Nataraja, Surya, Harihar, gandharvas and floral motifs, with scattered sculptures displayed around the temple precinct.

touristPlaces.name: Kutaghat Dam
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic reservoir near Ratanpur with boating amid forested hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kutaghat Dam lies close to Ratanpur, surrounded by low forested hills and calm waters — a favourite picnic stop on the Bilaspur heritage circuit. Its serene reservoir makes for relaxing afternoon visits.

touristPlaces.name: Bilasa Tal
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Cradle-shaped lake cradled by hills — a tranquil boating retreat in Bilaspur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bilasa Tal is Bilaspur's charming hill-cradled lake, offering leisurely boat rides and peaceful waterfront strolls. Its still waters mirror the surrounding greenery, making it an idyllic spot to unwind near the city.

touristPlaces.name: Kali Mandir (Bilaspur)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Famous Kali temple in the heart of Bilaspur, crowded during Navratri.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Kali Mandir of Bilaspur is a much-revered city shrine to goddess Kali, drawing steady daily devotees and enormous Navratri crowds. Its important location makes it an easy stop while exploring the city centre.

touristPlaces.name: Devrani-Jethani Temples, Tala
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A twin-peak Kalachuri temple pair at Tala — the Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Devrani and Jethani temples of Tala are among the purest Kalachuri art in India. Beyond the carvings, the living culture includes the annual Shiva-rath procession when the whole village carries the idol through paddy fields — a medieval pageant still replayed today.

touristPlaces.name: Achanakmar Shiva Shrine
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A mossy forest shrine inside tiger country, worshipped by herders.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Deep inside the Achanakmar reserve, a small Shiva ling carved from a single rock receives offerings of ghee and jungle flowers from passing tribals and shepherds. The priest is a Gond villager who continues an oral tradition of forest reverence — the hidden culture of the sal forest.

touristPlaces.name: Madku Dweep (Jatmai Holi)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: An island with temple ruins amid river-fed forest near Bilaspur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Madku Dweep is a little-visited island in the Kharun backwaters, ringed by forest and dotted with the remains of medieval shrines. During Jatmai Holi the island glows with bonfires and folk drums — a festival preserved by the surrounding farming villages.

touristPlaces.name: Bilaspur Chhattisgarhi Bhoj (Ramanuj Nagar)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Local food house famous for spirulina chila, aam-kaddu and khurma.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A no-frills eatery where a working lunch means a thali of rice, dal, chutney, seasonal vegetables and the famous chenna khurma sweet. Regulars argue over whether the spirulina chila or the jaggery chila should win the morning session.

touristPlaces.name: Budhwari Market Street Food
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Bilaspur’s old market lane crowded with chaat, bhajiya and lassi stalls.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Budhwari bazaar has fed Bilaspur for a century. Its evening stalls — dal pakauri, bhatti ke sabzi, jalebi, and the creamy bilasputi lassi — turn the lane into the city’s living room. The atmosphere is loud, friendly and utterly local.

touristPlaces.name: Kargi Road Brahmi Nadi Ghat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A peaceful river ghat where farmers bathe at dawn and egrets fish at dusk.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A hidden ghat on the Brahmi river with no tourist infrastructure at all — just stone steps, old trees, and village rhythm. Sunrise here is a meditation: fog lifts, women set lamps afloat, and kingfishers work the shallows.

touristPlaces.name: Ratnapur Sufi Dargah & Baoli
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A medieval baoli and dargah preserving a shared saintly tradition.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This baoli (stepped well) and dargah near old Ratnapur shows the syncretic culture of Chhattisgarh — a saintly tradition honoured by both Hindu and Muslim villagers who light lamps together on Thursday evenings.

name: Bastar
desc: Land of waterfalls, tribal culture and dense forests

touristPlaces.name: Chitrakote Waterfalls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: India's widest waterfall — the "Niagara of India".
touristPlaces.fullDesc: India's broadest waterfall, stretching nearly 300 meters during monsoon.

touristPlaces.name: Tirathgarh Falls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Multi-tiered 300-feet waterfall inside Kanger Valley National Park.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Stunning 300-foot waterfall on the Kanger River inside the national park.

touristPlaces.name: Kanger Valley National Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Spectacular national park with caves, waterfalls, and rare wildlife.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: 200 sq km of lush biodiversity with caves, waterfalls, and rare Bastar Hill Myna.

touristPlaces.name: Kotumsar Cave
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of the longest natural caves in India with eyeless cave fish.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: 1,327-meter cave with stalactites and rare eyeless cave fish species.

touristPlaces.name: Bastar Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: 200-year-old royal palace of Bastar kings — now a heritage museum.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Built in 1891, partial museum featuring royal artifacts and tribal art.

touristPlaces.name: Anthropological Museum Jagdalpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Fascinating museum dedicated to Bastar's 12 tribal communities and their art.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Showcases life-size tribal displays, traditional weapons, ornaments, musical instruments, and artworks of the Gondi, Maria, and Muria tribes.

touristPlaces.name: Dalpat Sagar Lake
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Large historic lake in Jagdalpur — popular for boating and evening walks.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Historic lake built during the Bastar kingdom era. Surrounded by a garden and popular for boating.

touristPlaces.name: Mendri Ghumar Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hidden horseshoe waterfall — one of Bastar's most photogenic spots.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beautiful waterfall on the Indravati river tributary. Less visited than Chitrakote.

touristPlaces.name: Bastar Dussehra Ground
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The venue of the world-famous 75-day Bastar Dussehra — a unique tribal festival.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Unlike conventional Dussehra, Bastar celebrates its grand festival for 75 days in Jagdalpur, centred on the Danteshwari deity with intricate rituals, bamboo chariot processions, and tribal dance. The festival ground and the historic wooden Ratha are cultural treasures of global significance.

touristPlaces.name: Kudumkhara Eco Tourism
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Interconnected natural ponds and caves near Jagdalpur — a hidden Bastar gem.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kudumkhara in the Bastar hills is a striking natural site with a series of interconnected ponds and cave chambers forged by centuries of water flow. Locals consider it sacred, and the emerald water surrounded by misty forest makes it one of Bastar’s best-kept secrets.

touristPlaces.name: Jagdalpur Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly tribal market in Jagdalpur — Chhattisgarh’s richest craft bazaar.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Jagdalpur Sunday Haat is where Gond and Maria tribals from surrounding villages bring forest produce, handmade metalwork, woodcraft, and colourful weaves. It is the best place to see the famous Bastar art forms and bargain directly with artisans.

touristPlaces.name: Maa Danteshwari Shakti Peeth (Dongargarh Circuit)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The queen goddess of Bastar — temple of the royal family and the people.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Danteshwari temple is the political and spiritual heart of Bastar. Its culture fuses royal worship (the Raja- hat as her chief devotee) with folk ritual: during Bastar Dussehra, the goddess travels through the palace courtyard and town in a ceremonial palanquin, uniting hundreds of tribal groups in one festival.

touristPlaces.name: Mama Bhanja Temple, Barsoor
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A relic of the 10th-century twin-Ganesh complex — the preserved twin icons now moved.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Barsoor’s old temple precinct, with the two great Ganesh icons relocated to the town square, still holds the hidden temple culture of the region: carved doorways, a ruined Sabha Mandap, and an oral tradition of the midnight devta dances once held at the shrine.

touristPlaces.name: Jawanga Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A 12-metre jump hidden in Kanger Valley — fewer visitors than Chitrakote.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Jawanga falls is the sleeper of Bastar’s waterfalls: a white curtain spilling into a jade pool within sal and bamboo forests. The hidden culture nearby includes Gond outrigger myths of the water spirit and seasonal honey-gathering beats still practised.

touristPlaces.name: Chitrakote Ghat and Boat Village
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sunset boat rides beneath the grand horse-shoe falls.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beyond the obvious viewpoint, the Chitrakote ghat launches bamboo-and-nylon boats that swing under the falls for a mist-soaked close-up. The boatmen are Halba villagers whose families have run the crossing for generations.

touristPlaces.name: Bailadila Hills Homestay Fold
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest-fringe cafe run by a tribal cooperative serving Gond coffee and chila.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: On the road towards the iron-ore hills, a tiny cooperative cafe serves coffee grown on tribal land, gond-style breakfasts and mahua tea. Money stays in the village, and the walls are hung with Dhokra and wood art tours can buy direct.

touristPlaces.name: Jagdalpur Ghongha Haat (Weekly)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The unhurried village haat away from the tourist haats.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ghongha village’s weekly haat is where Muria and Halba families actually trade — not for tourists: tamarind, honey, iron implements, and hand-rolled herbs. It is the most honest window into Bastar’s living market culture.

touristPlaces.name: Bastar Signature Podi Roti Thali (Nagar Gate)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Highland home-style thali centred on podi roti and chousela.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Named for the folded rice roti of the plateau, this home-kitchen restaurant serves chousela (rice bread) with red millet curry, madia-pej porridge, and a chutney line-up of chilli, groundnut and forest coriander. Recipes are handed down from tribal grandmothers.

name: Durg
desc: Industrial hub with temples and cultural richness

touristPlaces.name: Uwasaggaharam Parshwa Teerth
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Exquisitely carved Jain temple — one of the most beautiful in the region.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Magnificent Jain temple with detailed marble carvings and intricate relief work.

touristPlaces.name: Maitri Bagh Zoo
touristPlaces.shortDesc: 53-acre zoo and botanical garden — built as a symbol of Indo-Soviet friendship.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Includes zoo, botanical garden, toy train, and boating on a central lake.

touristPlaces.name: Tandula Dam
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic reservoir surrounded by forested hills — great for birdwatching.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Built across Seonath River in 1921. Excellent for migratory birdwatching in winter.

touristPlaces.name: Ganga Maiya Temple Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Popular riverside temple dedicated to Ganga Maiya on the Shivnath river.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beloved temple with large annual Chhath Puja celebration drawing thousands of devotees.

touristPlaces.name: Surya Cinema Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Long-running cinema hall loved by Durg-Bhilai moviegoers.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Surya Cinema is one of Durg’s most enduring single-screen theatres, connecting generations of local film lovers. Paired with the city’s famous street food, a movie night here is a classic Chhattisgarhi urban outing.

touristPlaces.name: Bhilai Maitri Bagh Lakefront
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Boating lake at Maitri Bagh with gardens — a relaxed family spot.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beyond the famous zoo, Bhilai’s Maitri Bagh offers a serene artificial lake with paddle boating set in landscaped gardens. The “Indo-Soviet friendship” park grounds are a favourite for quiet evening strolls and family picnics.

touristPlaces.name: Hotel Fire Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Popular Durg hotel with a lively rooftop restaurant and bar.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hotel Fire Park is a well-known hospitality landmark of Durg offering comfortable rooms and one of the city’s favourite dining terraces. Its restaurant is a sought-after venue for corporate meals, family dinners, and weekend celebrations.

touristPlaces.name: Nukkad Tea Cafe (Nehru Nagar, Bhilai)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Socially-inclusive cafe chain in Nehru Nagar with murals, live music and great food.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bhilai branch of Nukkad Tea Cafe in Nehru Nagar East is renowned for its vibrant wall murals, floor-cushion seating, and a small performance stage. Built on the same inclusive social mission as the Raipur cafes, it employs differently-abled youth and serves delicious teas, coffee and snacks.

touristPlaces.name: Shakti Temple Circuit, Bhilai
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Durg-Bhilai’s venerated goddess and old-town family temples.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The temples of Durg town centre preserve a distinct clan-and-goddess culture: each old family worships its own kul-devi in miniature shrines, while big festivals like Navratri bring the whole city to the main Shakti temples. The syncretism of steel-city migrants and agrarian natives makes this circuit unique.

touristPlaces.name: Nagpura Hanuman Temple Caves
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A walled shrine built into a low hill — Hanuman temples of the old town.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: On the Durg–Bhilai road, a small hill hosts a rambling Hanuman temple complex partly hewn into the rock. Local legend places the shrine on an old traders’ route, and folk memory holds that merchants slept within the cave walls. Its aura is quiet, incense-filled, and very old.

touristPlaces.name: Shivnath Historical Ghat, Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Old stone ghat on the Shivnath with medieval steps and village boats.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Durg’s Shivnath ghat has largely been bypassed by new bridges, leaving an untouched riverside terrace of dark stone steps, cremation-temple pavilions and fishing boats. Dawn aartis and the winter fog over the river hold an old-town tranquillity.

touristPlaces.name: Bhilai Steel City Kannamal Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The green and rose-garden heart of steel-city Bhilai.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kannamal Park is where Bhilai’s immigrant-worker history meets leisure: manicured rose gardens, a boating lake and families from a dozen languages enjoying the evening air. The adjoining Civic Centre’s shops and cafes reflect the cosmopolitan culture of the steel township.

touristPlaces.name: Chhattisgarhi Dal-Bhaji Stall (Civil Lines Durg)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: An evening stall famous for dal-kachauri and green chilli pakauri.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This decades-old Civil Lines stall has no menu and no chairs — just a hot kadhai, rivers of chutney, and the city’s best dal-kachauri. The queue of office-goers at six PM is the real institution.

touristPlaces.name: Family Bhoj Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Durg’s best-known thali house for fara, chila and gud khurma.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A cheerful mid-sized family restaurant where a full Chhattisgarh bhoj — fara, chila, bafauri, sweet-sour kadhi, pumpkin and jaggery khurma — travels from kitchen to table in minutes. Portions are generous, prices are townsfolk-friendly.

touristPlaces.name: Mahadev Temple, Deobaloda
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A 13th-century Kalchuri Shiva shrine by the Charoda rail line — built, they say, in six months.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Deobaloda’s Mahadev temple is an ASI-protected Kalchuri-era gem that almost nobody visits on purpose. Local legend holds that it was raised in just six months — hence its old name "6-Maashi" — and that a tunnel once ran from its tank towards the temple town of Arang. Boar- and deer-hunt reliefs ring the sanctum walls, and on Mahashivratri the surrounding villages gather with a small fair.

touristPlaces.name: Dhamdha Chaturbhuji & Shiva Temple Group
touristPlaces.shortDesc: State-protected medieval temples strung through Dhamdha, the ancient Gond citadel of Dharmdham.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Dhamdha, once the fort-citadel of a Gond clan, preserves a tight group of carved stone temples — the Shiva shrine and the four-armed Chaturbhuji temple among them — protected by the state. The old Prachin Kila mound still shoulders the town, and worship continues quietly among the tombs and ruins along the Durg–Bemetara road. Few who pass the town ever stop; the carvings reward those who do.

touristPlaces.name: Ancient Vishnu Temple, Banbarad
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A state-protected medieval Vishnu temple standing alone among Banbarad’s fields.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Banbarad’s ancient Vishnu temple is a protected monument that time has largely forgotten: a quiet stone shrine ringed by farmland on a sandy village lane. Carved panels survive around the sanctum, where village women still light lamps on Purnima evenings. It is the stillness of the place that stays with you — a deep, flat Durg plain, one small temple, and no crowds anywhere.

touristPlaces.name: Nagdev Temple, Nagpura
touristPlaces.shortDesc: An ancient serpent-lord shrine behind Nagpura’s lanes — away from the famous Jain tirth.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: While Nagpura is celebrated for the Uwasaggaharam Parshwa Teerth, the village also guards an old Nagadev (serpent-lord) temple under state protection. Cobra motifs frame its small stone sanctum, and village families still tend and decorate the shrine around Nag Panchami. Incense-heavy, shrublined and crowd-free, it is the quietest corner of a town that always draws pilgrims for the wrong reasons.

touristPlaces.name: Langurveer Mandir, Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: India’s one-of-a-kind temple to Langurveer — the dark-faced Hanuman — tucked in old Durg bazaar.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Langurveer temple is Durg’s hidden peculiarity: a shrine to the fierce, dark-faced Hanuman form called Langurveer, which by all accounts is the only dedicated Langurveer temple in India. Worshippers thread through the bazaar lanes all day with offerings, and devotion here is intense and distinctly local. No grand entrance announces it — ask any shopkeeper to point the way.

touristPlaces.name: Chandi Mandir, Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Old Durg’s beloved goddess temple off the main bazaar — at its strongest during Navratri.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Behind the busy Gaya Nagar lanes, Chandi Mandir holds one of the city’s most loved Chandi (Durga) idols. On ordinary days it is a quiet street shrine of incense and bells; during Navratri the narrow approaches fill with bhajan processions and vendors’ carts. It is landmarked in locals’ memories rather than any tourism map — the city keeps it to itself.

touristPlaces.name: Dakshinmukhi Hanuman Temple, Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A rare south-facing (Dakshinmukhi) Hanuman shrine in the heart of Durg.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In a walled courtyard off the old city core, Durg’s Dakshinmukhi Hanuman temple faces south — the fierce orientation devotees seek for protection and calm. The shrine is small and the faith intense: mornings draw office-bound worshippers, and Hanuman Jayanti queues spill into the street. Its quiet fame stays resolutely local.

touristPlaces.name: Jagannath Mandir, Durg
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The old city’s Jagannath temple, where Rath Yatra brings Durg’s lanes alive.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Durg’s quiet Jagannath temple sits in a corner of the old town with a modest shikhara and a small courtyard. Its annual Rath Yatra is a true local affair — a hand-pulled chariot, families in festival clothes, and halwa being served along the route — while the rest of the year the sanctum hums with daily aarti. A rare devotional corner of the steel city, almost never on itineraries.

name: Rajnandgaon
desc: Cultural and religious centre with famous hilltop temples

touristPlaces.name: Dongargarh — Bambleshwari Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hilltop Shakti shrine perched 1,600 feet high — accessible by ropeway.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of the most revered pilgrimage sites with panoramic views. Ropeway or 1,100 steps.

touristPlaces.name: Rajiv Lochan Mandir, Rajim
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Magnificent 8th-century Vishnu temple at the holy Triveni Sangam.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Nagara-style masterpiece at the confluence of three rivers — the Prayag of Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Khutaghat Dam
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beautiful dam with forest surroundings perfect for a nature retreat.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Scenic dam on the Sheonath River surrounded by dense forest, popular for picnics.

touristPlaces.name: Ambaghat Viewpoint
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dramatic mountain pass viewpoint on the Ambagarh road.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Spectacular viewpoint offering panoramic views of forested valleys.

touristPlaces.name: Gandai Temple Complex
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Cluster of ancient Kalachuri-era temples at Gandai — a hidden heritage treasury.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Gandai (once Mahapura) near Rajnandgaon contains the ruins of a dozen medieval Shiva temples with exquisite stone carvings. Forgotten by mainstream tourism, it is a rewarding stop for history lovers exploring the region.

touristPlaces.name: Rajiv Lochan Mel Ranga
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Local festival and riverside gathering at Rajim — vibrant folk tradition.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Rajim and Rajnandgaon host lively melas (fairs) centred on the Mahanadi ghats, with folk dance performances, handicraft stalls, and puppet shows celebrating the region’s agrarian-tribal culture.

touristPlaces.name: New City Mall Rajnandgaon
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Modern retail complex for fashion, electronics, and dining in the city.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: New City Mall brings a contemporary shopping experience to Rajnandgaon with clothing brands, electronics outlets, a supermarket, and fast-food counters — increasingly the social hangout for the city’s youth.

touristPlaces.name: Dongargarh Maa Bamleshwari Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A 1,600-step climb to a goddess temple skirting the rails of the Rajnandgaon hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Dongargarh’s Bamleshwari deity draws lakhs of pilgrims, yet its culture is deeply domestic: families climb together, chant the goddess’s bhajans, and offer coconut-and-vermillion. The ropeway weaves above the same forest path generations of villagers have walked.

touristPlaces.name: Rustic Baiga Shrine, Baghnadi Valley
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest shrine of the Baiga tribe deep in the Baghnadi valley.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hidden up a forest trail live the worship of the Baigas — the original forest people — who honour this small rock shrine with new-moon rituals. The hidden culture preserved here (honey-offering rites, animist taboos, herbal vows) is among the oldest in Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Kududam Ho Village Lakeland
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A still lakeland with island groves at the edge of Rajnandgaon forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kududam Ho is a stretch of dam-formed water where low forested islands break the surface. Fishing camps, kingfisher-rich shallows and an absence of facilities make it a true hidden spot for slow travellers.

touristPlaces.name: Rajur Food Joints (Kududam-Chhuri)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Riverside eatery famous for bhindi-machli (river fish) and salebhaja.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: On the road to the dam, local kitchen sheds cook the day’s river catch — crisp fried goongi and katla steaks — with coarse rice and pej. Fishermen eat here at dawn; the fish is that fresh.

touristPlaces.name: Mauji Bazaar Evening Market
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Rajnandgaon’s old bazaar alive with silver, snacks and smells.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Mauji Bazaar captures the town’s trading character — hand-woven chanderi, silver craft, laurel mithai shops and the evening snack wave of bhajiya and chai. It is the social spine of Rajnandgaon after work hours.

name: Korba
desc: Power capital with stunning natural waterfalls

touristPlaces.name: Kendai Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Stunning natural waterfall plunging through forest rocks.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Breathtaking waterfall in dense forests with natural pools and excellent trekking trails.

touristPlaces.name: Pali Shiv Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient Shiva temple complex with historic sculptures and serene setting.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Group of ancient Shiva temples from the Kalachuri period with fine stone carvings.

touristPlaces.name: Hasdev Bango Dam
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Massive reservoir dam on the Hasdeo river — stunning sunset destination.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of the largest dams in Chhattisgarh with spectacular views.

touristPlaces.name: Korba Shopping Complex
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Central market complex of Korba for daily shopping and street food.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The shopping complexes around Korba’s Geetankutir Chowk serve as the district’s commercial heart, with textile shops, electronics, and buzzing evening food stalls serving local chaats and vada.

touristPlaces.name: Korba Station View Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Heritage railway park with a museum — a family weekend spot.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Korba’s railway and station area has been developed with a small park and display of vintage locomotives, offering a pleasant family outing and a glimpse into the rail history that shaped this power city.

touristPlaces.name: Kudurmal Temple Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Rich sculpture of an ancient temple hidden in Korba fields.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kudurmal preserves some of the densest mythological panels in central India — but almost no one comes. The temple hidden culture (stone ladies, mating animals, celestial dancers) shows how storytelling covered every surface of medieval Chhattisgarh temples.

touristPlaces.name: Hasdeo Aranya Forest Temple Groves
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Shiva shrines inside the Hasdeo forest where elephants pass the walls.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Within the Hasdeo Aranya, herding tribes maintain forest shrines where the stone lingams are anointed with forest honey. The hidden culture is one of coexistence: the shrines are avoided by wildlife corridors yet visited weekly by village youth.

touristPlaces.name: Pondi-Dongri Baand Falls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A little-known cascade in the reservoir hills of Korba.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Pioneer-Baand stream south of Korba forms a pretty seasonal fall that locals guard like a secret. Summer bathers of the empty pools and the wet-season roar both belong to the same hidden place that never appears on signboards.

touristPlaces.name: Jai Stambh Chowk Family Bhoj
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Power-plant town favourite for chhalla rice, pej and chicken bartha.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Korba’s industrial workforce (thousands strong) fills this eatery for a working-man’s thali: heavy rice, soupy pej, chicken bartha and baskets of chila. Prices are set for shift workers, so portions are heroic.

touristPlaces.name: Kosabadi Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly tribal market in the Korba coal-belt forest fringe.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kosabadi’s weekly haat draws Baiga and Gond communities selling lac, honey, tussar thread and livestock. Unlike the showpiece bazaars, this one is work — raw, seasonal and vivid.

name: Surguja
desc: Hill station, Mini Tibet and ancient caves

touristPlaces.name: Mainpat Hill Station
touristPlaces.shortDesc: "Mini Tibet of Chhattisgarh" — scenic plateau at 3,700 ft.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Breathtaking plateau at 3,781 feet with Tibetan refugee settlements, monasteries, meadows.

touristPlaces.name: Tiger Point Mainpat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dramatic cliff-edge viewpoint with panoramic forested valley views.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Most popular viewpoint in Mainpat with spectacular sunrise and sunset vistas.

touristPlaces.name: Ramgarh Hill
touristPlaces.shortDesc: India's oldest surviving manmade theatre — the 2,300-year-old Sitabenga Cave.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Contains the Sitabenga Cave dating to 300 BC and Jogimarha Cave with Brahmi inscriptions.

touristPlaces.name: Tatapani Hot Springs
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Natural geothermal hot springs with believed medicinal properties.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Geothermal springs beside the Mahanadi River, popular during Makar Sankranti.

touristPlaces.name: Semarsot Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dense forested sanctuary rich in leopards, bison, and rare birds.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: 430 sq km sanctuary in the Surguja hills with excellent biodiversity.

touristPlaces.name: Ulta Pani Mainpat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Fascinating natural optical illusion — water appears to flow uphill.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A gravity-defying natural illusion near Mainpat where water and vehicles seem to roll uphill.

touristPlaces.name: Ambikapur Nakshatra Garden
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Landmark city park with themed gardens, fountain, and an open-air amphitheatre.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Nakshatra Vatika in Ambikapur is an award-winning urban green space with gardens themed around the 27 nakshatras, a musical fountain, and an amphitheatre hosting cultural programmes. It has transformed Ambikapur’s civic life.

touristPlaces.name: Ambikapur Heritage Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Royal palace of Surguja now hosting visitors — heritage stay.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The historic Surguja (Ambikapur) palace complex, architecture of the erstwhile princely state, lets visitors experience royal spaces and museum galleries that document the tribal and regal past of north Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Mini Tibet Monastery (Mainpat)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Tibetan Buddhist monastery settled by Tibetan refugees in Mainpat.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Tibetan settlements of Mainpat established a vibrant Buddhist community with prayer wheels, stupas, and monastery courtyards perched on the plateau. Visiting gives a window into a culture thousands of miles from home.

touristPlaces.name: Cafe Deiji (Ambikapur)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Top-rated cosy cafe on Godhanpur Road serving speciality coffee and snacks.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Cafe Deiji on the way to Vasundhara Vihar is one of Ambikapur’s best-loved cafes, offering speciality coffee, quick bites and a warm, comfortable atmosphere. A favourite hangout for students and families in Surguja.

touristPlaces.name: Mahamaya Temple, Ambikapur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The goddess temple of Surguja town — bazaars, bell towers and fairs.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Mahamaya temple anchors Ambikapur’s weekday rhythm: at dawn flower-sellers set up prayer arcs, at dusk the bell-drums call the town home. Its Devi culture blends Rajput-era temple ritual with the folk song of the Pathalgadi hills.

touristPlaces.name: Sita Bengra Caves
touristPlaces.shortDesc: An ancient rock-cut cave complex with inscriptions near Ambikapur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Sita Bengra rock-cut caves carry inscriptions and sculptures from the ancient Hahaikkar heritage of Surguja. The hidden culture here is palpable: oil lamps flicker where priests once chanted, and the surrounding hamlet still performs seasonal cave rites.

touristPlaces.name: Tamor Pingla Hidden Forest Loop
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest-road loop inside tiger country less walked than the main safari.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beyond the gate safaris, the quieter forest roads of the Tamor-Pingla belt pass salt-licks, herd halting places, and villagers who know every elephant by name. This is the hidden, slow way to experience the corridor.

touristPlaces.name: Baba Chowk Sweet House, Shankarpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The town’s oldest sweet house famous for khurma and rabri mithai.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Three generations of the same family run this Shankarpur landmark on Surguja’s sugar-farming belt. Khurma, peda, rabri and seasonal mohna sweets come out in big brass trays each morning and are gone by three.

touristPlaces.name: Ambikapur Bazaar Evening Walk
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The uphill lanes of Ambikapur’s old market — craft, snacks and noise.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ambikapur’s umbrella-and-aluminium bazaar lanes host chandelier craft, terracotta, and carving tools from the woodworking hamlets around. The evening snack train of kachauri and jalebi turns the climb into a festival.

touristPlaces.name: Semarsot Hidden Beech Grove
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest clearing where honey-gatherers set their seasonal hives.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In the Semarsot forest block, tribal families keep age-old beehive groves on silk-cotton trees, harvesting honey with smoke and ritual thanks. Visiting with the village shows a living wild-food culture untouched by galleries.

name: Mahasamund
desc: Ancient archaeological treasures and heritage sites

touristPlaces.name: Sirpur Archaeological Site
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Once-magnificent ancient city on the Mahanadi — 12,000+ artifacts.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Capital of South Kosala kingdom with temples, monasteries, and palaces from 6th–8th centuries.

touristPlaces.name: Laxman Temple Sirpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Remarkably preserved 7th-century brick temple — a masterpiece of ancient architecture.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of the finest examples of early Nagara architecture, entirely of burnt brick with intricate carvings.

touristPlaces.name: Buddha Vihar Sirpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient Buddhist monasteries showing the region's vibrant Buddhist past.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Complex of monasteries and stupas from 7th–9th centuries with exceptional bronze Buddhas.

touristPlaces.name: Surang Tila Sirpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Massive underground Shiva temple excavated at Sirpur — a hidden marvel.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Extraordinary underground Shaiva temple discovered at Sirpur with a tunnel and several chambers.

touristPlaces.name: Rajim Kumbh Ghat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Holy riverfront ghat at Rajim where three rivers meet — Chhattisgarh’s Prayag.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Rajim, known as the Prayag of Chhattisgarh, hosts a famous Kalpavas Mela in Magh at the Triveni of Mahanadi, Pairi, and Sondur rivers. The bathing ghats and evening aartis create one of the most spiritual atmospheres in the state.

touristPlaces.name: Mahasamund Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly market of Mahasamund with local produce and handloom.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Mahasamund’s weekly haat is a vibrant village marketplace where farmers and artisans sell vegetables, handloom saris, and forest produce — a lively slice of Chhattisgarh’s rural economy.

touristPlaces.name: Rajim Rajiv Lochan Temple & Kumbh
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The sacred Vishnu town at the Mahanadi–Pairy confluence.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Rajim is Chhattisgarh’s Prayag: three rivers meet, temples line the banks, and the annual Rajim Kumbh draws folk boatmen, mendicants and musicians. The temple culture here keeps alive scriptural worship alongside the river-fair of the common people.

touristPlaces.name: Sirpur Seigniorage (Lakshmana Temple) Yoga Circuit
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The grand brick temple of Sirpur — Buddhism, Shaivism and Balaji in one site.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sirpur was a great 7th-century seat of Buddhist learning whose brick shrines — including the superb Lakshmana temple — mix Buddhist, Shaiva and Vaishnava imagery. Its hidden culture is first-rate archaeology with barely a dozen visitors on most days.

touristPlaces.name: Rajim Hidden Ghat Herranch
touristPlaces.shortDesc: An old bathing ghat with carved steps away from the festival grounds.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Downstream of the main temples, Rajim keeps a crumbling 18th-century ghat with lion-head spouts and worn panels of the river goddesses. Dawn lamplight and winter fog make it look like an old miniature painting.

touristPlaces.name: Basana Bafauri Bhoj
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Family kitchen restaurant famous for bafauri, usal and guvava chutney.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This Mahasamund dining room plate-ups the Mahanadi belt’s comfort food: steamed bafauri (gram-flour cutlets), spicy usal, and a raw mango– guvava chutney that locals defend ferociously. Home-style, honest, and famous for its vegetarian thali.

touristPlaces.name: Pithora Art Village Walks
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Village walls painted in living Pithora wall-art tradition.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In the villages around Mahasamund, house walls bloom with Pithora paintings — ritual art of the Oraon–Gond pantheon executed in lime and colour. A guided walk past the painted facades is a museum without walls.

name: Dhamtari
desc: Nature, wildlife and water sports paradise

touristPlaces.name: Gangrel Dam (Ravishankar Sagar)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Chhattisgarh's largest dam — popular for water sports.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Largest dam in Chhattisgarh across the Mahanadi offering boating and water sports.

touristPlaces.name: Madku Dweep
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Forested river island with ancient Shiva temples — accessible only by boat.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: River island on the Sheonath with ancient Shiva temples and mystical atmosphere.

touristPlaces.name: Sihawa Shringhi Rishi Ashram
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient ashram — believed to be the birthplace of Mahanadi river.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sacred ashram of sage Shringhi Rishi where the Mahanadi river originates in the Sihawa hills.

touristPlaces.name: Rudri Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sacred 12th-century temple complex at Rudri — a hidden heritage site.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Rudri near Dhamtari houses ancient stone temples dating to the 12th century with intricately carved pillars and deities. Tucked away from tourist circuits, it offers peaceful heritage exploration amid farmland.

touristPlaces.name: Sihawa Hills Viewpoint
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Panoramic viewpoint over the Sihawa range — origin of the Mahanadi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Sihawa hills rise dramatically above the plains, offering expansive viewpoints over the forested range where the Mahanadi river originates. Trek-friendly and increasingly popular with weekenders from Raipur.

touristPlaces.name: Gangrel Water Sports
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Boating, kayaking, and jet-ski on Chhattisgarh’s largest reservoir.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Ravishankar Sagar at Gangrel has developed into Chhattisgarh’s premier water-sports destination, with boating, kayaking, and speedboat rides across the vast reservoir. Family-friendly and scenic.

touristPlaces.name: Gangrel Dam Backwater Pools
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A big scenic reservoir ringed by forest and farmland.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Gangrel reservoir spreads over forest-fringed water with slow boating, angling spots, and winter bird gatherings. It is Dhamtari’s weekend heart and the source of much of the region’s irrigation.

touristPlaces.name: Nagi-Bird Corridor (Hidden Fen)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A hidden wetland corridor known to birders, not signboards.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: South of the reservoir, a string of private tanks draws painted storks, cranes and migratory ducks each winter. The hidden spot is a farm-track circuit that rewards dawn-lovers with uncommon bird lists.

touristPlaces.name: Kurud Shiva Temple Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient Shiva-shrine remains in the rice belt near Kurud.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Old Nagara stones of a Shiva temple rest among rice fields near Kurud, still receiving coconut offerings from ploughmen. The quiet continuity — a village keeps the puja while the archaeology rots politely — is the hidden culture of the plains.

touristPlaces.name: Fara-Chila Dhaba (SH9 Belt)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Highway dhaba famous for fara baskets and khatta-bhatta thali.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This unmarked dhaba on the Nagri road serves what every Dhamtari family prays for on a long drive: a full khatta-bhatta thali, baskets of fara with chutney, and churma in ghee. The khatta (tamarind-tangy) base is Dhamtari’s signature cooking.

touristPlaces.name: Dhamtari Haat Fridays
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly rice-belt market with pottery, grain and village gossip.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Each Friday Dhamtari’s haat colonises a field’s edge: potters stack bhuna (unglazed pots), grain merchants heave jaggery sacks, and farm families turn the morning into a festival of trade and talk.

name: Gariyaband
desc: Spiritual and natural wonders in forested terrain

touristPlaces.name: Jatmai Ghatarrani Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Breathtaking waterfall-temple complex — Shakti shrine beside cascading falls.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Jatmai Temple dramatically beside a multi-tiered waterfall in a forested gorge.

touristPlaces.name: Udanti Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Critical sanctuary for the endangered Wild Buffalo of Chhattisgarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: 347 sq km sanctuary — one of the last strongholds of the Wild Buffalo.

touristPlaces.name: Ghatarrani Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Multi-tiered waterfall adjacent to the Jatmai Temple.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The waterfalls at Ghatarrani cascade over several tiers through forested gorge.

touristPlaces.name: Rajim Kumbh Fair
touristPlaces.shortDesc: North Chhattisgarh’s grandest temple fair at the Triveni Sangam.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Rajim Kumbh (Magh Purnima Kalpavas Mela) is a month-long festival at Gariyaband’s Rajim ghats blending ritual bathing, temple processions, folk music, and crafts. A deep cultural immersion for researchers and devotees alike.

touristPlaces.name: Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Thriving tiger and bison sanctuary off the main tourist path.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Barnawapara is a compact but rich sanctuary with significant tiger, leopard, and wild buffalo populations, plus deer and peafowl. Fewer visitors than Achanakmar makes it a delightfully intimate safari experience.

touristPlaces.name: Rajiv Nagar Ghuisarnath Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A revered Nath shrine ringed by forest in the Gariyaband hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Ghuisarnath temple sits in a wooded depression at the foot of the hills — a Nath yoga lineage site where lintel-lamps still burn. Its culture couples austere Shaiva values with the mushroom-and-honey harvests of the surrounding villages.

touristPlaces.name: Krishna Tumar (Hidden) Temple Clearing
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A wild temple-clearing deep in the forests below the hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beyond the main shrine, a smaller rock-shiva clearing is reached by a forest path; villagers light lamps on new moons. The hidden culture here is a living animist Shaivism — the stone is family, the forest is sacred.

touristPlaces.name: Hills of Gariaband Border Watch Point
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A high ridge trail with views over the bunds and forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The eastern hills of the district (toward Odisha) hide a ridge-loop walked by herders, not trekkers. From the top, the bund-dam landscape, sal forest and far blue hills stretch to the horizon — worth every step.

touristPlaces.name: Gariaband Village Chula-Na thela
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A chulha (clay-stove) kitchen serving Brahmi-fresh parathas and mahua chai.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Runs on a clay stove in the village bazaar, serving ghee parathas, millet raab, and mahua chai out of steel tumblers. No signage, no menu — just the warmest kitchen in the hills.

name: Kabirdham
desc: Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh with ancient temples

touristPlaces.name: Bhoramdeo Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: "Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh" — 11th-century Shiva temple with erotic carvings.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Three 11th-century temple complex with exquisite carvings in verdant forest setting.
touristPlaces.bestTime: October to March; March dance festival

touristPlaces.name: Kawardha Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Magnificent 1939 Indo-Saracenic palace — now a heritage hotel.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Stunning palace by Kawardha royal family with landscaped gardens and royal heritage.

touristPlaces.name: Bhoramdeo Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dense forested sanctuary surrounding the ancient Bhoramdeo temple complex.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Maikal Hills sanctuary home to leopards, sloth bears, and rich birdlife.

touristPlaces.name: Madwa Mahal
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Charming 14th-century wedding pavilion temple near Bhoramdeo.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Small temple pavilion built in the 14th century with carvings rivalling those of Bhoramdeo.

touristPlaces.name: Chirbhitti Temple Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient ruined temple site with sculpted remains near Kawardha.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Scattered medieval temple ruins and carved stone remains near Kawardha document the region’s rich religious past. For archaeology buffs, these lesser-known sites are as rewarding as Bhoramdeo.

touristPlaces.name: Kawardha Nartiya Jain Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Elegant Jain temple at Nartiya with fine stone carving.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Jain temple cluster at Nartiya is noted for its richly carved sandstone architecture and serene setting. A significant pilgrimage site that also rewards lovers of temple sculpture.

touristPlaces.name: Bhoramdeo Temple Elegance
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh — a 11th-century Shiva gem in green hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bhoramdeo is Chhattisgarh’s greatest temple: a compact Nagara Shiva shrine covered in celestial dancers, elephants and mythology, set in forest ringed by ponds. Its culture runs from the ancient Kalachuri ritual to the folk song nights staged in the surrounding orchards.

touristPlaces.name: Chaurasi Temple Hidden Carvings
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The oldest Bhoramdeo-era temple with its crown still imperfect, hidden by trees.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Chaurasi temple, older than Bhoramdeo and tucked among trees, still wears its unfinished crown. Its quiet supine Simha-thresholds and un-plastered walls show the medieval artisans’ original working surface — a hidden art-history lesson.

touristPlaces.name: Jijgaon Dheeji (Restored) Heritage Pond
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A village pond ringed by old trees where painted storks winter.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Jijgaon’s thousand-year pond is a hidden wetland: old ficus groves, a festival tank, and flocks of painted storks and cormorants each winter. Chicken-shack eateries on the far bank serve the district’s best satpuda chicken curry.

touristPlaces.name: Kabirdham Fish Thali (Lal Chanda Bhoj)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The reservoir-belt kitchen famous for singara fish fry and dudha rice.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Near the dam-fed lakes, this family bhoj serves the day’s catch — singara and kaira fries, steamy rice, and the sweet dudha (milk-sweet) finish. Prices stay village-fair and the fish comes from coracles ferried that morning.

name: Jashpur
desc: Tea gardens, tribal culture and scenic waterfalls

touristPlaces.name: Kailash Gufa (Cave)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sacred natural cave temple dedicated to Lord Shiva amid serene forest.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Natural cave with Shiva linga formations in dense forests, ideal trek destination.

touristPlaces.name: Rajpuri Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beautiful waterfall cluster near Jashpur — most picturesque in the district.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Cascades over tiered rock formations into crystal-clear pools in highland forests.

touristPlaces.name: Jashpur Tea Gardens
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic tea estates in the Jashpur highlands — rare in central India.
