touristPlaces.fullDesc: Small tea estates with scenic walks and tea cultivation learning opportunities.

touristPlaces.name: Rani Jharna Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Serene hidden waterfall in thick forests — a photographer's delight.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Tranquil waterfall surrounded by dense canopy, rarely crowded, ideal for nature lovers.

touristPlaces.name: Kunkuri Church
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Asia's second-largest Catholic church — a magnificent Gothic structure.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The massive Catholic diocese church at Kunkuri is one of Asia's largest and most beautiful Gothic churches.

touristPlaces.name: Bagicha Waterfalls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Twin cascades in the Bagicha forest — a scenic hidden spot.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bagicha in Jashpur is home to twin waterfalls that tumble over rock shelves into clear pools, surrounded by sal forests. A popular picnic destination that remains blissfully uncrowded on weekdays.

touristPlaces.name: Kunkuri Catholic Church Grounds
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Revered cathedral town of Kunkuri with peaceful church surroundings.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kunkuri is a major centre of Christianity in central India, centred on one of Asia’s grandest Catholic churches. The tranquil campus, gardens, and the community’s warmth make it a unique cultural visit in tribal Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Jashpur Palm Eco-Tourism
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Eco camp amidst Jashpur’s hill forests with tribal homestays.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Jashpur’s eco-tourism initiatives offer nature camps and tribal homestays in the hill villages, combining forest walks, folk dance evenings, and organic farm-to-table meals. An immersive, responsible travel choice.

touristPlaces.name: Kailash Gufa (Hidden Cave Shrine)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A mountain cave where Shiva is worshipped in darkness, dripping water.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kailash Gufa is a natural cave shrine in the Bagicha hills, reached by steep forest steps. Inside, a lingam stands under cave drips; devotees climb weekly and the Oraon–Christian mountain villages share the reverence — one of Jashpur’s most moving cultural fusions.

touristPlaces.name: Bagicha Coffee-and-Smoko Point
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A hill-top tea-and-coffee shack above the Jashpur plateau.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A wooden shack on the plateau rim pours robust filter coffee and long-stirred chai to sunrise watchers and mist enthusiasts. Winter mornings the whole valley below is a sea of fog — the view is the food.

touristPlaces.name: Manora Hidden Falls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A twin cascade in the Duhu–Manora forest ridge, off every map.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Manora falls spill quietly through black rock in the tribal forest — one more of Jashpur’s beautiful hidden drops. Local girls string wildflowers into the pool at Chaitra; the rest of the year it is yours alone.

touristPlaces.name: Jashpur Pine Hill Crest Trail
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The cool crest-line walks through pines and coffee patchwork.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Jashpur plateau’s crest trails cross pine copses, coffee and orange groves, and hill-village clusters served by the famous Jharkhand-minute forest roads. It is Chhattisgarh’s most un-Chhattisgarh landscape.

touristPlaces.name: Kunkuri Tribal Craft Market
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Bamboo, iron and honey market of the north plateau tribal belt.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kunkuri’s weekly haat brings Oraon and Munda communities with basketwork, honey, iron tools and hand-looms — a working market, not a craft show. The drum-choirs of community celebrations sometimes roll through the lanes.

name: Korea
desc: Amrit Dhara falls and dense elephant forests

touristPlaces.name: Amrit Dhara Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Spectacular 90-foot waterfall on the Hasdo River through dense forest gorge.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Amrit Dhara ("stream of nectar") with Shiva temple complex nearby, popular on Mahashivratri.

touristPlaces.name: Chirimiri Hill Station
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Pleasant coal-town hill station in Korea with cool climate and forest trails.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Charming hill town at 2,000+ feet with scenic forest walks and cool retreat atmosphere.

touristPlaces.name: Hasdeo Aranya Forest
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Vast biodiversity-rich forest — habitat of elephants and tigers.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of central India's largest forests, critical habitat for elephants, tigers, 100s of birds.

touristPlaces.name: Koriya Palace (Baikunthpur)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic palace of the Korea princely state at Baikunthpur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Koriya royal palace at Baikunthpur reflects the architecture and dynasty of the former Korea state. Its semi-renovated halls and museums give an insight into north Chhattisgarh’s princely heritage.

touristPlaces.name: Baikunthpur City Market
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Busy local market of Baikunthpur for tribal crafts and produce.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Baikunthpur’s bazaar is the trading hub of Korea district, where tribal communities sell forest honey, turmeric, and handmade items. An authentic shopping and people-watching experience.

touristPlaces.name: Bhairava Ji Temple Cave, Baikunthpur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest cave shrine with a howling vent — a hidden Shaiva site.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hidden in the Baikunthpur forest, a cave where air howls through a rock vent is worshipped as a Bhairava shrine. The hidden culture here is austere: animal-masked votives, iron tridents, and deep forest silence between visits.

touristPlaces.name: Jharga Coal-Age Views (Hidden Ridge)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A ridge overlooking the Son basin and the coal-mining fabric of Korea.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: North of Baikunthpur, a farm ridge rises over the Son valley with whale-back hills stacked to the horizon — the mining terraces glitter like folded metal at dusk. No viewpoint exists; the villagers own the horizon.

touristPlaces.name: Baikunthpur Mithai Bhandar (Chandal Bhujji)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sweet house famous for khurma and the region’s chandal (gram) toffees.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This old Bhandar in Baikunthpur town has spooned out khurma, gujhia and seasonal chandal toffees since the princely-state days. Its jaggery-rich sweets reflect the sugarcane belt of northern Chhattisgarh.

name: Dantewada
desc: Danteshwari Shakti Peetha — the soul of Bastar

touristPlaces.name: Danteshwari Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of the 52 Shakti Peethas — the most sacred goddess temple of Bastar.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Most revered shrine in Chhattisgarh, centre of the 75-day Bastar Dussehra festival.

touristPlaces.name: Barsur Temple Complex
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient temple complex with a massive twin Ganesh idol from the 10th century.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Cluster of ancient Nagara style temples with a pair of Ganesh statues, 5 feet tall each, at Barsur.

touristPlaces.name: Bailadila Hills Viewpoint
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Iron-ore hills of Bailadila with dramatic ridge-line views.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bailadila iron-ore range dominates the Dantewada skyline, crisscrossed by mining terraces that create a surreal landscape. Viewpoints on the approach roads offer strong panoramas of this mineral heart of Bastar.

touristPlaces.name: Dantewada Tribal Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly haat where Dantewada’s tribal communities trade and socialise.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Dantewada haat is a colourful weekly gathering of Gond, Bharia, and Halba tribals selling forest goods and crafts. It is also a celebration of community life — music, food, and laughter.

touristPlaces.name: Barsur Ganesh Temple Retired Landscape
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The twin Ganesh icons and the old temple plaza of Bargarh taluk.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bargarh (Barsur) was a mighty 10th-century capital; its twin five-foot Ganesh statues stand in the temple plaza while older ruins sprawl around. The hidden culture survives in battle-goddess myths and the grave formal dances performed in Bason village.

touristPlaces.name: Mheelan Thekadar Temple Remains
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Undergrowth-covered temple remains down the Dantewada reaches.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sculpted stones and a broken shikhara lie half-claimed by forest near Mheelan — a forgotten site of the Bastar kingdom’s frontier. Its hidden culture is the mystery itself: who carved, who left, who still ties a thread on the worn deity each full moon.

touristPlaces.name: Geedam Ho-Hat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A weekly communal market of the southern Bastar tribal belt.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Geedam’s weekly haat is a true frontier market: honey, mahua oil, iron implements and bright handlooms traded under awnings by Gond–Halba farmers. It is the economic pulse of a block most travellers never reach.

touristPlaces.name: Bailadila Quarry (Kiran) Point
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The iron-ridge panorama above the tunnels and terraces of Kirandul.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Kirandul overlook peers across the layered iron-orange terraces of the Bailadila mines, a landscape of staggering scale. Evening light paints the ridges rust-gold — a vista few Indian landscapes match.

name: Kanker
desc: Jungle camps, heritage palace and tribal trails

touristPlaces.name: Kanker Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic 1937 palace — now a heritage hotel overlooking the Dudh River.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Gracious heritage property with forest surroundings and royal experience.

touristPlaces.name: Kanker Jungle Safari
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Guided jungle safaris — rich in leopards and 150+ bird species.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Excellent biodiversity with leopards, spotted deer, sambar, sloth bears, and birds.

touristPlaces.name: Dudh River Rafting
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Gentle river rafting on the scenic Dudh River through forested gorges.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: White water rafting on the Dudh River through scenic forested terrain near Kanker.

touristPlaces.name: Maa Danteshwari Temple, Kanker
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient goddess temple in old Kanker town — a spiritual anchor.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Maa Danteshwari temple maintains a serene presence in Kanker town, a significant Shakti shrine of the Bastar belt. Navratri brings the town alive with processions and tribal dances.

touristPlaces.name: Sankri Village Eco Stay
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Heritage tribal village homestay amid Kanker hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sankri and neighbouring tribal villages near Kanker welcome visitors into their traditional homesteads for curated homestay experiences — forest walks, bamboo crafts, and Gond cuisine prepared by host families.

touristPlaces.name: Khariar Temple (Hidden Panchayat Shrine)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A village shrine with a bell-tree and folk-marriage ritual.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In Khariar’s panchayat belt, a shrine wears hundreds of tiny bells tied by newlyweds and mothers — a vow-culture hidden from every guidebook. The bells ring a village’s private prayers on every passer-by wind.

touristPlaces.name: Anthariagarh Fort Mound
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Fort ramparts and a hidden lake on the Kanker ridgeline.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Anthariagarh’s broken ramparts crown a rock ridge over the Kanker valley, with a hidden tank (lake) fed by forest springs at its base. Sunrise from the rampart stones is peerless and entirely unseen.

touristPlaces.name: Kanker Recipe Table (Resort-District Local)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Bastar-forest thali of mahua-infused gravies and millet breads.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Serving what the Kanker forests cook, this tableside kitchen plates up ragi-pitha, millet-pej, mahua-tangy chutneys and wild-turmeric lentil curries — the cuisine of the tribal belt translated for the traveller’s plate.

touristPlaces.name: Bhatgaon Village Rooftop Café (Informal)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A homestay rooftop terrace café above a tribal village courtyard.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: On a homestay roof in Bhatgaon village, the host family serves chai and hot chila to a band of travellers as the village drums for Nagpuri songs below. It is hospitality, not a business — the best dish is the conversation.

name: Kondagaon
desc: Tribal crafts capital and gateway to Bastar art

touristPlaces.name: Crafts Bazaar Kondagaon
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Vibrant market showcasing authentic Bastar Dhokra metalwork and woodcraft.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Crafts capital of Bastar with Dhokra casting, iron craft, terracotta, and bamboo work.

touristPlaces.name: Keshkal Ghati
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dramatic mountain valley with 7 hairpin bends and forest panoramas.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Most scenic mountain pass in Chhattisgarh, favourite for photographers and road trippers.

touristPlaces.name: Bell Metal Village Dokra
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Visit working Dhokra artisan families — watch the 4,000-year-old craft live.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Villages near Kondagaon where Dhokra craft families still practise the ancient lost-wax bronze casting technique.

touristPlaces.name: Umargaon Iron Craft Village
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Home of Bastar’s delicate 'nakkal' iron sculptors.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Umargaon near Kondagaon is famous for the extraordinary 'silk-soft' iron sculptures crafted by local artisans — a Bastar art form of international renown. Watch masters shape deer, tribes, and deities from single iron sheets.

touristPlaces.name: Kondagaon Dhokra Shilpi Sanstha
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Cooperative of Dhokra artisans preserving the lost-wax craft.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Kondagaon artisan cooperatives bring together hundreds of Dhokra families, standardising quality while keeping the 4,000-year-old lost-wax technique alive. A model of tribal entrepreneurship and craft preservation.

touristPlaces.name: Keshkal Ghati Hidden Viewpoints
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The switchback valleys of Keshkal with secret pause-points.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Keshkal Ghati’s hairpins are famous; its side tracks to emerald valley bowls are not. Walk down any unpaved turn-off and the Mand-River basin folds below like a green theatre.

touristPlaces.name: Bodeli Gond Ho (Haat) Morning
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The famous Bodeli haat where every Bastar craft is laid out.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bodeli’s weekly haat is the classic Bastar market: dhokra, woodwork, terracotta, jewellery, and bell-metal across hundreds of stalls. Tourists and artisans mix here as equals — the best of Bastar’s art economy.

touristPlaces.name: Taragaon Iron-Craft Village (Hidden)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beyond Umargaon, the quieter iron-sculpting hamlets.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: While Umargaon gets the tour buses, Taragaon and its neighbours quietly work the same nakkal iron technique in family forges. The hidden art here is unchecked by galleries — raw, brilliant and cheap.

name: Balod
desc: Hidden gems — sacred temples, forest waterfalls & serene rural landscapes

touristPlaces.name: Ganga Maiya Temple, Jhalmala
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Revered riverside goddess temple at Jhalmala — a sacred spot of deep local faith.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ganga Maiya Temple at Jhalmala is a beloved riverside shrine dedicated to Ganga Maiya.

touristPlaces.name: Tandula Dam & Reservoir
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Major scenic dam on the Tandula river with backwaters, migratory birds and boating.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Spread over 1,100 hectares, the Tandula reservoir is one of the most scenic dams in Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Rural Haat (Weekly Tribal Market)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Vibrant weekly tribal market — a living, breathing cultural experience.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The rural haats of Balod district are among the most authentic cultural experiences in Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Quitab Nala Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Refreshing forest waterfall and stream near Balod.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Quitab Nala is a picturesque seasonal waterfall where locals flock on weekends. The stream-side setting among teak forests makes it ideal for short treks and picnics.

touristPlaces.name: Dalli Rajhara Mines View
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Iron-ore mining town views — land of the 1920 labour movement.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Dalli-Rajhara, a historic iron-mining town of Balod district, is etched in India’s labour history through its famous 1960s workers’ movement memorialised across the region. The terraced mines create a unique industrial landscape.

touristPlaces.name: Lal Bhaonta (Hidden) Cave Shrine
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A red-stone cave shrine of the Satnami and Gond villages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A short walk from the Dalli-Rajhara granite fields, a red-creeper cave shelters a revered stone. Villagers paint it in seasons of sowing and harvest — the hidden culture of the agricultural calendar, not the calendar of tourism.

touristPlaces.name: Sankara Hidden Falls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A stone-spill waterfall in the Sankara forest, off the maps.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sankara’s forested stream makes a pretty two-step fall that no board names. Locals bathe before Magha Purnima fairs, then the pool goes quiet until the rains return.

touristPlaces.name: Kosmi Balod Fal (Jaggery) Corner
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A winter corner famous for gud-paise and rod-chokha juice.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In the cane belt around Balod, a roofless winter stall boils fresh jaggery and pours gud-paise over crumbled roti with raw onion. It is a December institution you will not find listed anywhere.

name: Baloda Bazar
desc: Turturiya pilgrimage site and ancient heritage

touristPlaces.name: Turturiya Ashram
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sacred ashram believed to be the birthplace of sage Valmiki, author of Ramayana.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Deeply revered pilgrimage site on the Balm river with ancient temples and tranquil surroundings.

touristPlaces.name: Giroudpuri Dham
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sacred birth site of Guru Ghasidas — founder of the Satnami movement.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Major pilgrimage centre for the Satnami community. A beautiful ghat on the Mahanadi.

touristPlaces.name: Deorbija Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient stone temple complex at Deorbija with fine carvings.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Deorbija in Baloda Bazar district preserves centuries-old temples with exceptionally fine stone carving. Secluded and rarely visited, it rewards travellers willing to detour off the highway.

touristPlaces.name: Simga Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Traditional weekly market at Simga for local produce.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Simga’s weekly haat is a vibrant marketplace of the Baloda Bazar plains where farmers bring fresh produce and artisans sell handloom and ironware. A window into everyday Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Sanwakot Bhavani Temple Ridge
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A fort shrine of the Mahanadi bend with riverside steps.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bhavani temples above the Sanwakot bend keep the time of the river: morning aarti facing east over the Mahanadi, evening lamps for the boatmen’s return. The fort walls around them belong to a forgotten Rajput outpost.

touristPlaces.name: Pithora Wall Trail, Kutki
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Village Pithora murals beyond the main sanwakot circuit.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kutki and its hamlets paint Pithora horse-goddess murals on every new bride’s wall. Walking the lanes with local elders decodes a folk cosmology that fills museum catalogues but lives here on lime and ochre.

touristPlaces.name: Baloda Bazar Sunday Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sunday’s river-plain market — grain, poultry, crafts and noise.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Baloda Bazar town’s Sunday haat floods its central maidan with everything from milled grain mountains to terracotta granaries and handlooms. The pace is agricultural, the energy enormous.

touristPlaces.name: Kasdol Village Chai & Chokha Corner
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Village chokha (smoked brinjal mash) with rice cosmere.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A Kasdol kitchen garden stall smokes brinjal over rice-straw, mashes it with mustard oil and green chillies, and serves rice-paper rotis by the stack. It is the rural raw lunch of the Mahanadi belt.

name: Balrampur
desc: Waterfalls, forests and tribal culture in north Chhattisgarh

touristPlaces.name: Tatapani Hot Springs Balrampur
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Natural hot water springs revered for medicinal properties near Balrampur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Geothermal springs on the Son River banks, believed to cure skin ailments.

touristPlaces.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sprawling national park shared with Madhya Pradesh — tiger and elephant habitat.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Part of the Sanjay-Dubri Tiger Reserve, home to tigers, leopards, gaurs, and wild dogs.

touristPlaces.name: Dipadih Temple Complex
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ruined medieval temple complex in the forests of Kusmi — an archaeological wonder.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ancient temple ruins dating to the medieval period near Kusmi, Balrampur.

touristPlaces.name: Ramanujganj Ropeway & Hills
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hill viewpoint near the district share of the Ramgarh caves.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ramanujganj, on the Jharkhand border of Balrampur district, is a scenic tribal belt with rolling hills whose viewpoints unfold wide forested panoramas. Peaceful and dramatically different from the plains.

touristPlaces.name: Kusmi Traditional Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly tribal market at Kusmi for crafts and forest produce.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Kusmi haat is where the region’s tribal communities exchange lac, honey, baskets, and livestock. A short and authentic detour that reveals trade and craft traditions of north Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Ramgarh Hill Votive Shrines
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient monastic hill with rock-cut temples above the Ramgarh catchment.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Across the Ramgarh ridge (shared with Jharkhand) sit rock-cut vestibules once used by monks. Local worship of the carved reliefs keeps a devotional thread alive on a hill the big tour operators never reach.

touristPlaces.name: Sarmura Tanr (Hidden Falls)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A wooded cascade in the Ban Sagar catchment, off Serengighat’s route.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: At Sarmura Tanr, forest water slides over black slabs into an amber pool that swallows the midday heat. The hidden culture: village women flower the pool for the rains’ return in Asarh.

touristPlaces.name: Balrampur Tribal Prawa (Staple) Bhoj
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Adiwasi thali of rotis, millet semai and mahua chutneys.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This village-kitchen-style bhoj plates the north-district tribal diet: prashad (millet) semai, mahua chutney, petha-side gourds and forest greens. Cooks are grandmothers from the Kutia-Kondh belt; recipes shift with the harvest.

touristPlaces.name: Ramanujganj Border Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A market that is the only thing between two states’ villages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ramanujganj haat pulls vendors from both Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand — drums, iron, fox-control tools and hard sweets across one fairground. The two-state mingling is the whole charm.

name: Bemetara
desc: Agricultural heartland with temples and rural heritage

touristPlaces.name: Navagarh Fort
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient fort with historical significance in the Seonath river plains.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Fortification remnants from the medieval era with surrounding moat and ancient stonework.

touristPlaces.name: Sita Mandir Deorbeeja
touristPlaces.shortDesc: 12th-century Sita Mandir with exquisite stone carvings — a hidden archaeological gem.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beautifully carved 12th-century temple at Deorbeeja dedicated to Sita.

touristPlaces.name: Durg-Bemetara Rural Lake Circuit
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Cluster of serene village lakes ideal for winter birdwatching.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bemetara’s countryside is dotted with village tanks that attract migratory waterfowl through winter. A low-key lake circuit rewards birdwatchers with spoonbills, cormorants, and teal away from crowded parks.

touristPlaces.name: Saja Basti Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Local village temple with rich folklore and peaceful surroundings.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Saja Basti in Bemetara is known among locals for its ancient shrine and quiet rural setting. It provides a genuine, un-commercialised look at village faith in the Chhattisgarh plains.

touristPlaces.name: Sahaspur Lakha Temple Stretch
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Brick-temple remains along the Sahaspur plain — a hidden group.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Scattered brick shrines along the Leve basin carry rare 11th-century terra-cotta plaques. The village ploughs around them, festivals honour them, and archaeology barely knows them — a genuine hidden heritage.

touristPlaces.name: Berla Din (Hidden Festival Tank)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A large ritual tank where the Din festival turns the water to lamps.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Berla’s tank doubles each Din festival as a lamp-plaza: thousands of clay lamps float, and the Deora dance circles the bundes. On ordinary days it is a serene duck-water mirroring the winter sun.

touristPlaces.name: Gandai Bafauri Stall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Street bafauri stand famous for gram-fritters and tri-colour chutneys.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: At a four-post stall in Gandai bazaar, bafauri (gram cakes) bubble by the hundred in murky oil and arrive with three chutneys — tamarind, mint, and the cracked red chilli. It is Bemetara’s great cheap eat.

name: Bijapur
desc: Remote Bastar frontier with pristine rivers and tribal life

touristPlaces.name: Indravati National Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Remote tiger reserve on the banks of the Indravati river.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of India's most remote parks, home to the wild buffalo, tigers, and barasingha deer.

touristPlaces.name: Indravati River Camping
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Riverside camping on the pristine Indravati — one of India's most remote experiences.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Camp beside the Indravati River in pristine natural surroundings.

touristPlaces.name: Bhairmgad Fort
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic fortification associated with the Bhairam deva shrine.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bhairmgad and the surrounding Bastar frontier preserve ancient fort walls and a revered Bhairam shrine. These remote sites offer a rare glimpse into the region’s martial and tribal past.

touristPlaces.name: Pamed Tribal Villages
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Traditional tribal settlements of the remote Pamed block.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Pamed is one of the most remote and pristine tribal blocks of Chhattisgarh, home to Gond and other indigenous communities preserving elaborate rituals and forest livelihoods. Visits are strictly guided and permission-based.

touristPlaces.name: Mamma Gandi Festival Dancers (Hidden Tribal Stage)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Authorised village circuit where Gond dancers perform the Mamma festival.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Around the remote Purgei and Madded belts, permitted village visits can coincide with the Mamma or Dantewada ceremonial dances — hours of drum, mask and hornbill feathers in stone-paved courtyards. A rare cultural depth reserved to responsible travel.

touristPlaces.name: Indravati Islands (River Camp Reach)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sand-island camps on the Indravati, reachable by coracle.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Between the Park’s banks, sand islands surface in winter with tamarisk groves and coracle landings. Camping on such an island with a permitted operator is a frontier adventure few Indians have done.

touristPlaces.name: Bhairmgad Fort Gate Trees
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A fort gate guarded by a banyan whose roots entomb ritual goddess stones.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bhairmgad’s ruined gate is knotted by a great banyan; inside its root curtain, village women plant goddess stones for fertility each Jeth. The fusion of fort, forest and faith is pure Bijapur.

name: Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi
desc: Newest district with forested hills and tribal beauty

touristPlaces.name: Pendra Hill Station
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Cool hill station in the Maikal range with pleasant climate and forest walks.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Pleasant town on the Chhattisgarh-Madhya Pradesh border with scenic forested surroundings.

touristPlaces.name: Doodh Dhara Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Milky-white cascade through basalt rocks — a scenic hidden gem.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Milky waterfall pouring over black basalt, named for its milk-like appearance, set in dense forest.

touristPlaces.name: Pendra Eco Camps
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Forest eco camps in the Maikal range with trekking trails.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Pendra’s forest department runs eco-camps in the lush Maikal hills offering simple cottages, guided nature trails, and campfire evenings. A quiet retreat away from the plains’ summer heat.

touristPlaces.name: Marwahi Temple Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient temple remains scattered in Marwahi’s forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Around Marwahi, medieval temple ruins and sculpted stone fragments lie half-buried in the forest, a testament to the region’s bygone Hindu kingdoms. Intriguing for heritage explorers with local guidance.

touristPlaces.name: Pendra Caves (Hidden Sagar Shrine)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A cave-temple at Pendra where Shiva drips with hill water.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Pendra’s hill caves hold a natural Shiva shrine where drips plate the lingam year-round. The humble ritual culture—tilak and bell, hill grass and silence—has survived without door-priests or donation boxes.

touristPlaces.name: Marwahi Fruit & Fish Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Saturday haat where the Gond villages trade forest fruit and hill-fish.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Marwahi’s Saturday haat is rice-belt commerce on a smaller, hillier scale: hill mangoes, mahua cake, tamarind blocks and crates of river-fish from the Son tributaries. Its aromas are the memory.

touristPlaces.name: Pendra Ras-Wadi (Jhark) Bhoj
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Hill-wadi restaurant famous for ras-wadi moong and forest dal.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: This no-frills eatery at the Pendra-Pandan road junction plates the plateau’s comfort food: ras-wadi (fluffy moong dumplings in thin curry), forest dal, and gud churma. Truckers’ favourite, cook’s reputation.

name: Janjgir-Champa
desc: Ancient Shaktipeeth and Mahanadi riverfront heritage

touristPlaces.name: Vishnu Temple Janjgir
touristPlaces.shortDesc: 12th-century unfinished Vishnu temple — an architectural marvel of the Kalachuri era.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Massive 12th-century Vishnu temple that was never completed, with extraordinary stone carvings.

touristPlaces.name: Champa Shivnath River Ghats
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Serene ghats on the Shivnath river — ideal for sunrise and spiritual walks.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beautiful bathing ghats lined with temples along the Shivnath river.

touristPlaces.name: Nariyara Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient Vishnu temple at Nariyara — a sculptural gem.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The 12th-century temple at Nariyara showcases the exquisite carving tradition of the Kalachuri era, rivalling the better-known Janjgir sites. Secluded and atmospheric, it rewards those who seek it out.

touristPlaces.name: Champa City Mall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Modern retail complex in Champa with stores and food court.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Champa has embraced modern retail with a city mall offering fashion, electronics, and fast-food outlets. It’s the social epicentre for locals between shopping and cinema.

touristPlaces.name: Shivrinarayan Temple & Haate-Paa
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The trident-festival temple of the Mahanadi — Shiva’s spear fair.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Shivrinarayan pairs river-bend worship with the incredible Haate-Paa trident festival, when iron tridents are borne in procession and blessed mid-river, drawing the whole farming basin. Its culture is pure folk-Shaivism at scale.

touristPlaces.name: Kharod Dharampur Caves (Hidden)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient rock-cut chambers above the Dharampur reach.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Hidden above the Dharampur stretch, weathered rock-cut chambers and panels puzzle locals as much as scholars. Vine-shaded and monk-quiet, they are the district’s best secret.

touristPlaces.name: Akaltara Adabs Stretch (Hidden Fossil Site Feel)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A relaxing riverside reach near Akaltara with fossil-hunt finds.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Akaltara cut exposes river sediments where patient fossickers find ancient shells and brittlestars. Beyond the fossils, the reach is a peaceful picnic terrace under date palms.

touristPlaces.name: Champa Khurma & Sauna (Street) Corner
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Evening corner famous for champa khurma and hot sauna-ni.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Champa’s oldest sweet-and-namkeen corner fries saffron-tinted khurma, pustoli, and serves sauna-ni (hot jaggery-nut powder) in paper cones. Winter evening classic.

name: Khairagarh-Chhuikhadan-Gandai
desc: Music heritage, hills and forest landscape

touristPlaces.name: Indira Kala Sangit Vishwavidyalaya
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Asia's first music and arts university inside a royal palace — a cultural gem.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Established in 1956, this unique university is housed in the historic Khairagarh palace.

touristPlaces.name: Khairagarh Fort Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Elegant royal palace now housing the famous music university.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beautiful heritage palace of the Khairagarh princely state with gracious architecture.

touristPlaces.name: Khairagarh Irrigation Dam
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic irrigation reservoir near Khairagarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The irrigation dam around Khairagarh forms a pleasant water body ringed by fields and scrub forest, popular for picnics and short walks. The calm setting contrasts with the town’s musical bustle.

touristPlaces.name: Nartiya Jain Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Exquisitely carved Jain shrine at Nartiya.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Jain temples at Nartiya in the Gandai belt feature ornate carved mandapas and deities. A respected pilgrimage site that also fascinates lovers of medieval Chhattisgarhi sculpture.

touristPlaces.name: Nartiya Jain Temple Festivals
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ornate Jain temples near Gandai with lively ria-vat ritual fairs.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Nartiya Jain complex weds carved mandapas to vivid festival culture — processions, folk bands and the community feasts of the Jain Gudiya belt. Its scale of ritual catches everyone by surprise.

touristPlaces.name: Chhuikhadan Hidden Ration Pudu (Shrine Tank)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A village tank-shrine with ancient mother-goddess reliefs.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: At a farm tank near Chhuikhadan, weathered mother-goddess reliefs squat at the water’s edge, chalked fresh each new moon. The hidden culture of the Deori–Gond villages keeps the small stones alive.

touristPlaces.name: Khairagarh Music-Walk (Rajasthan Bahubali Café)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A café corner beside the music university where ragas meet chai.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Across the music university gate, tea-stall masters pour chai with tabla cycle in their heads — evenings turn into impromptu jam circles of students. The music, not the menu, is the point.

name: Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur
desc: Coal-mining hill town with forests and scenic valleys

touristPlaces.name: Hasdeo Valley Viewpoint
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Panoramic viewpoint over the vast Hasdeo river valley and forested hills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Spectacular viewpoint offering sweeping views of the Hasdeo Valley with forested ridgelines.

touristPlaces.name: Sonmuda Valley
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Origin point of the Son river — a sacred and scenic destination.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Son River emerges from the Sonmuda plateau; the valley is peaceful and rarely visited.

touristPlaces.name: Manendragarh Viewpoint
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic overlook across the coal-belt valleys of Manendragarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Manendragarh and its surrounds offer dramatic views over deep valleys and mining terraces along the Son River frontier with Madhya Pradesh. Vistas are strong especially in the monsoon when everything is lush.

touristPlaces.name: Chirimiri Baba Dham
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Local shrine at Chirimiri hill station with scenic trail.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The 'Baba' cave-shrines around Chirimiri hill station are deeply venerated by the local mining communities. Short forest trails to these shrines mix faith with scenic walks.

touristPlaces.name: Bharatpur Forest Blocks
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dense forest blocks of the old Bharatpur estate.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The forested blocks of the Bharatpur region remain rich in wildlife and scenic teak stretches. Quiet drives here are a rewarding way to experience north Chhattisgarh’s wilderness.

touristPlaces.name: Manendragarh Dakshinini (Hidden) Falls
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A lesser-known cascade in the Son-hill country west of the town.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In the folding hills toward the MP border, a seasonal fall named for its southern aspect spills into a bouldered amphitheatre. Coal-town families know it; signboards do not.

touristPlaces.name: Bharatpur-Branchi Temple Grove
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest temple-grove of the old Bharatpur estate.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bharatpur forests hide a small Shiva grove with an estate-era well and votive stones — the devotional fringe of the old princely outpost. Hunters-turned-guides tell the dynastic tales in the cool.

touristPlaces.name: Chirimirri Baba Cave Chai
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A pilgrims’ tea corner below the Chirimiri cave-shrines.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Below the cave shrines, a family stall pours chai and slices laddoo for the long climb back. Its bench is the whole town’s meeting point after the diyas are lit.

touristPlaces.name: Sonmuda Valley Panorama Base
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The mist-hollow where the Son begins; panoramas above the springs.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Below the springs, a grassy lip overlooks the upper Son cut winding through pines and gullies. Sunrise here is a fog-ballet that justifies the bumpy approach road.

name: Mohla-Manpur-Ambagarh Chowki
desc: Tribal heartland with forests, waterfalls and wildlife

touristPlaces.name: Ambagarh Fort Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient fort ruins atop a hill with commanding views over the plains.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ruins of a medieval hill fort offering panoramic views and historical significance.

touristPlaces.name: Mohla Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Secluded forest waterfall popular with locals for weekend visits.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Tranquil waterfall in thick forest, accessible by a short forest path.

touristPlaces.name: Manpur Tribal Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Weekly market where Manpur’s tribal villages converge.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Manpur haat is a colourful rendezvous of forest produce, iron tools, and woven baskets from surrounding tribal villages. An authentic cultural experience off every tourist map.

touristPlaces.name: Kuwakot Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Seasonal waterfall in the Chowki forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Kuwakot hosts a scenic seasonal waterfall within the Mohla-Manpur forests, drawing local families for monsoon picnics. A pleasant hidden spot for those exploring the tribal belt.

touristPlaces.name: Ambagarh Fort Crown Walk
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A hill-fort loop with village panoramas from the crown stones.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ambagarh’s fort crown offers a 360-degree balcony over the plains, tank-flecked farmland and far jungle. Post-monsoon, green water mirrors the sky; winter dawns add mist-layers.

touristPlaces.name: Manpur-Janakpur Hidden Lake Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A tank-shrine island in Manpur with village-water rituals.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: An island shrine rises from Manpur’s great tank; on Ganga-Dussehra the villagers pole a flower-laden raft to it. Regular days see kingfishers and buffaloes sharing the shore.

touristPlaces.name: Chowki Chula Murgi (Ngari)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Rustic kotwali bhoj famous for bamboo-grilled murga and jowar roti.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In central Chowki, a courtyard kitchen roasts chicken over white-hot bamboo samps, shaving garlic into the smoke, and serves it with jowar rotis. The fire-play alone is worth the detour.

name: Mungeli
desc: Achanakmar gateway and ancient temple heritage

touristPlaces.name: Achanakmar Tiger Reserve Buffer Zone
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Buffer zone entry point into the Achanakmar Tiger Reserve from Mungeli.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Excellent wildlife zone with tigers, leopards, wild dogs, and exceptional birdlife.

touristPlaces.name: Lormi Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beautiful waterfall near Lormi town on the edge of the Achanakmar forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Charming waterfall accessible from Lormi town, surrounded by bamboo and sal forest.

touristPlaces.name: Madmaheshwar Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient Shiva temple in the hills — a revered pilgrimage stop.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Ancient Shiva shrine in a scenic hilltop setting drawing pilgrims from across the region.

touristPlaces.name: Lata Kharvai Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Lesser-known cascade near Mungeli’s forest fringe.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Lata Kharvai area conceals a pretty seasonal waterfall in its bamboo-forested valleys. A lovely quiet alternative to the busier falls of the region.

touristPlaces.name: Deogarh Temple Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ruined ancient temples around Mungeli’s villages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Scattered medieval temple ruins around Mungeli’s villages bear carved lintels and deities recalling a prosperous past. Great for slow heritage wandering.

touristPlaces.name: Madmaheshwar (Hill) Shiv Temple Dawn
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A Shiva temple on the Mungeli ridge with festival bonfires.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Madmaheshwar temple anchors the ridge-town faith: small fairs at Mahashivratri, bonfires at Phagun, and the morning mountain air rinsed with temple bells. Its simplicity is its strength.

touristPlaces.name: Lormi-Lata Kharvai Hidden Stream Park
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A stream-canyon walk with rock pools west of Lormi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Below the falling stream’s park-ready pools, the canyon relaxes into an unmarked walk of rock-pools and bamboo light. Sunday picnics gather upstream; this stretch stays quiet.

touristPlaces.name: Mungeli Pej-Chila Corner (Station Road)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Morning corner famous for pej porridge and thin chila.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: At the station-road corner, old men plot the weather over pej (millet porridge), thin green-chilli chila and raw onion. It is Mungeli’s slow morning ritual and best cheap meal.

name: Narayanpur
desc: Remote Abujhmaad heartland with pristine forests

touristPlaces.name: Abujhmaad Forest
touristPlaces.shortDesc: One of India's last great unexplored forests — a biodiversity treasure.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Vast uncharted forest inhabited by the Abujhmaria tribe, rich in flora and fauna.

touristPlaces.name: Orchha Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Dense forest sanctuary with tigers and rich biodiversity near Narayanpur.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Part of the Indravati corridor with tigers, leopards, gaurs, and hundreds of bird species.

touristPlaces.name: Abujhmaria Village Visit
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Authorised cultural visits to Abujhmaria tribal settlements.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: With government permission, cultural visits to Abujhmaria villages offer an unparalleled window into indigenous communities.

touristPlaces.name: Narayanpur Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Remote weekly market of Narayanpur’s tribal heartland.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Narayanpur’s weekly haat is the social and economic hub of the Abujhmarh fringe, where tribal communities bring forest produce and craft. A rare window into indigenous Chhattisgarh.

touristPlaces.name: Bhairamgarh Shrine
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Revered Bhairam shrine in the Narayanpur forests.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Bhairamgarh shrine is a significant religious site for the region’s tribal communities, tied to harvest and fertility rituals. Its forest setting adds to its mystique.

touristPlaces.name: Orchha Sanctuary Meadow Corner
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A grassy clearing within the sanctuary where deer graze at dawn.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Inside the Orchha buffer, a seasonal meadow trapped between sal groves is the district’s best quiet wildlife moment: chital and peafowl at first light, and usually nobody else in earshot.

touristPlaces.name: Chhote-Dongar (Hidden) Temple Stones
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A boulder shrine on the Abujhmarh fringe with dry-forest ritual.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: At the fringe village of Chhote-Dongar, a small boulder-shrine receives the harvest vows of the Abujhmaria settlements. It is more a gateway marker than a temple — and it moves no one but those who live there.

touristPlaces.name: Bhairamgarh Supari Bhoj (Authorised Stay Kitchen)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A forest-fringed kitchen serving adiwasi feasts under permit.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: With district permission, small authorised homestay kitchens serve Abujhmaria staples — mahua-scented pulses, millet breads, bamboo-shoot chutney — around a courtyard fire. The food IS the cultural exchange.

name: Raigarh
desc: Cultural capital of Chhattisgarh with Chakradhar arts

touristPlaces.name: Raigarh Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Historic palace of the Raigarh royal family — patrons of Kathak dance.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Royal palace that was a hub of classical music and Kathak dance under Raja Chakradhar Singh.

touristPlaces.name: Gomarda Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Lush sanctuary with tigers, leopards and diverse wildlife near Raigarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: 277 sq km sanctuary with tigers, leopards, bison, and over 200 bird species.

touristPlaces.name: Singhpur Cave Art
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient rock art caves with prehistoric paintings and carvings.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Prehistoric rock shelter paintings near Singhpur — believed to be 10,000 years old.

touristPlaces.name: Chakradhar Samaroh Ground
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The annual theatre of Raigarh’s world-class Kathak dance festival.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Raigarh’s Chakradhar Samaroh is among India’s premier classical dance festivals honouring Raja Chakradhar Singh, hosting Kathak gurus and maestros each winter. The festival grounds become a cultural stage of national importance.

touristPlaces.name: Jutkili Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient stone temple with fine carvings in Raigarh district.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Jutkili preserves a beautiful old stone temple whose past favours the region’s medieval sculptural tradition. Secluded and tranquil, it invites unhurried exploration.

touristPlaces.name: Raigarh City Mall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Modern mall bringing brands and food court to Raigarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Raigarh’s expanding retail scene centres on a city mall complex with apparel stores, a multiplex cinema, and a food court — the go-to hangout for the city’s families and youth.

touristPlaces.name: Kharod Rajiv Temple, Raigarh (Hidden Reach)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A secluded temple reach below Raigarh’s ghats.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Below the town ghats, a quieter reach holds a small temple whose steps meet the water at boat level. Early mornings the ferrymen moor there, and the shrine stays curtain-lit behind low hulls.

touristPlaces.name: Gomarda Watch-Ramps
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Walk the forest watch-ramps of Gomarda for dawn wildlife.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Gomarda’s watch-ramps run over salt-licks and wallows used by leopard, gaur and wild dog. Dawn sittings with a naturalist read the sand like a newspaper — the park’s best slow experience.

touristPlaces.name: Kathak Chai (Chakradhar Samaroh Season Café)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Festival-season café where dancers sip chai beside the amphitheatre.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Each October–November the amphitheatre corner becomes a café of ghungroos and chai: young Kathak students, gurus and rasikas share the same long bench. Any evening of the festival, any conversation is a masterclass.

touristPlaces.name: Kharsia Signature Chilla-Dal (Raigarh Bhoj)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Raigarh thali of chilla-pakoda, forest dal and jaggery rabri.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A Raigarh family bhoj cooking the old court-towns style: crisp chilla-pakoda, forest-dal with wild turmeric, aubergine bhujas, and jaggery rabri to close. Portions honour the Maihar–Raigarh patron culture.

name: Sakti
desc: Newly formed district with temples and rural heritage

touristPlaces.name: Chandrahasini Devi Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Famous Shakti shrine on the banks of the Mahanadi river.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Highly revered goddess temple at the confluence of Mahanadi, Jonk, and Lath rivers.

touristPlaces.name: Mahanadi River Banks
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Peaceful Mahanadi riverfront for sunsets, fishing and picnics.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beautiful sandy banks of the Mahanadi River ideal for relaxed evenings and fishing.

touristPlaces.name: Maa Bamleshwari Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sacred local Shakti shrine in the Sakti plains.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The goddess temples of Sakti district, including local Maa Bamleshwari shrines, anchor the faith of the surrounding villages. Simple, serene, and intimately tied to the district’s folk traditions.

touristPlaces.name: Sakti Urban Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Local market complex for traditional and daily shopping.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sakti town’s markets mix modern shops with traditional trading lanes where cloth, groceries, and local sweet specialities are sold. A pleasant authentic town stroll.

touristPlaces.name: Lathian Shiva Temple Bend
touristPlaces.shortDesc: An ancient Shiva bend with a carved doorway in the Sakti fields.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: In the fields near Lathian, a carved temple doorway still opens toward the river though the superstructure is gone. Monsoon plough turns up terracotta sherds and memories of the old mother-goddess pujas.

touristPlaces.name: Sakti Mahanadi Bank Market
touristPlaces.shortDesc: The riverside bazaar strip of Sakti town with bathing ghats.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sakti’s river edge is commerce and ritual at once — ghat steps, boat-launches, and the daily market where farmers trade grain by the Mahanadi’s reach. Sunsets turn the sandbar into a fairground.

touristPlaces.name: Bamleshwari Seva Bhoj (Sakti)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Temple-town bhoj famous for khichdi-prasad and batata sabzi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Across the temple, this modest dining room serves the bhog-style meals pilgrims crave: simple khichdi, puffed jaggery laddoos and salt-sweet batata. The queue after aarti is part of the devotion.

name: Sarangarh-Bilaigarh
desc: Royal heritage palaces and riverside temples

touristPlaces.name: Sarangarh Palace
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Graceful palace of the Sarangarh princely state — a lesser-known royal gem.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Beautiful palace with Chhattisgarhi architectural style and rich royal history.

touristPlaces.name: Bilaigarh Temple Complex
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ancient cluster of temples in Bilaigarh town on the Mahanadi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Group of traditional temples with beautiful stone carvings along the Mahanadi riverbank.

touristPlaces.name: Bilaigarh Fort Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Medieval fortification remains at Bilaigarh on the Mahanadi.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bilaigarh’s ancient fort walls and gateways beside the Mahanadi recall centuries of riverine power. Atmospheric ruins ideal for photography and quiet history visits.

touristPlaces.name: Sheorinarayan Ghat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Sacred Mahanadi ghat and confluence of state border villages.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Sheorinarayan on the Mahanadi is a revered ghat and religious hub of the Sarangarh belt with ancient temples and an annual fair. Its riverside aartis are deeply spiritual.

touristPlaces.name: Sarangarh Kila Gun-Gallery Corners
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Palace gun-gallery stroll with river reach views.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The old milieu of Sarangarh palace includes an elevated gun-gallery walk whose windows frame the Bilaigarh reach and fields below. Few visitors climb it; the few are rewarded with the town’s best vista.

touristPlaces.name: Bilaigarh River Sand-Isle Temple
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A winter-only sand-isle shrine mid-Mahanadi near Bilaigarh.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Each winter the receding Mahanadi exposes a sand isle where a small Hanuman icon is re-established — and re-drowned by the monsoons. Villagers race to it by boat for Magha fairs; its temporary-ness is the devotion.

touristPlaces.name: Tandula-Kasdol Haat (Saturday)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Saturday haat of the Sarangarh farmland with hand-weaves.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Around Tandula and Kasdol, Saturday haats fill with hand-loom saris, earthen griddles, and the month’s grain trade. The hand-weave lane alone justifies the detour.

touristPlaces.name: Bilaigarh Dudh Murgi Bhoj
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Country-kitchen famous for dudh-murgi and litti-sukha.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: A family courtyard kitchen serves the Sarangarh belt’s two great claims: dudh-murgi (chicken poached with creamy jaggery milk) and litti-sukha, smoked to a coal whisper. It is a dinner worth the drive from anywhere.

name: Sukma
desc: Remote Bastar with Sabari river and tribal heritage

touristPlaces.name: Sabari River Tribal Trail
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Remote tribal rivertrail along the pristine Sabari (Sileru) river valley.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Sabari River forms the border with Andhra Pradesh; the tribal villages and forests are extraordinary.

touristPlaces.name: Minpa Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Stunning remote waterfall in the Sukma forests — a hidden natural jewel.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Rarely visited waterfall in pristine Sukma forest, best experienced with a tribal guide.

touristPlaces.name: Dornapal Tribal Village
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Authentic Muria Gond tribal settlement with traditional lifestyle and crafts.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: One of the more accessible Muria Gond villages, where traditional lifestyle and Gond art traditions are still alive.

touristPlaces.name: Konta Tribal Market
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Colourful weekly market at Konta near the Sabari river.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Konta’s weekly haat brings Dora, Koya, and Gond communities together for trade and celebration — forest produce, hand gourds, and woven items. One of the most authentic market experiences in the Bastar region.

touristPlaces.name: Maidu Camp Ruins
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Ruins of the historic Maidu police camp on the Sabari river.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: The Maidu locality along the Sabari retains historic camp structures and riverine scenery significant to the region’s colonial past and tribal resistance history. A thoughtful stop on an authorised river trail.

touristPlaces.name: Konta-Errabor Background Tribal Trails
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Authorised Muria trails beyond the road-lines, near Errabor.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: With permitted tribal guides, the old Muria trails south of Konta loop through gut-forest, bison wallows and village orchards. It is the untouched Sukma — forest, custom and silhouette, no spectacle.

touristPlaces.name: Sabari Boat-Reach Shrine
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A river-shore shrine on the Sabari reach, nurried by boatmen.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: On the Sabari’s sand edge, a tiny boatman’s shrine to the river goddess is re-whitewashed each spring before the fish-run. Coracle crews light lamps here for safe water — an authentic riverine faith.

touristPlaces.name: Sukma Signature Pej & Bhaji (Authorised Kitchens)
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Authorised local kitchen famous for pej and wild-veg bhaji.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Within approved stay programmes, tribal kitchens plate pej porridge, wild-bitter bhaji, millet rotis and smoked-gourd chutney. The setting is a courtyard; the seasoning is forest, sun and salt.

name: Surajpur
desc: North Chhattisgarh forests, rivers and wildlife

touristPlaces.name: Tamor Pingla Wildlife Sanctuary
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Remote sanctuary home to elephants, tigers, and leopards.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Part of the Chhattisgarh elephant corridor; pristine forests with tiger and elephant populations.

touristPlaces.name: Chhatauni Waterfall
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Beautiful seasonal waterfall in the Surajpur forests — a local favourite.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Attractive waterfall flowing through forest rocks, popular for day excursions from Surajpur town.

touristPlaces.name: Bhainsamundi Skywalk
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Scenic elevated viewpoint in the Surguja foothills.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Bhainsamundi in Surajpur offers an elevated vista over forested valleys and the Surguja hills — a serene nature viewpoint drawing weekend visitors.

touristPlaces.name: Surajpur Urban Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: Town market of Surajpur selling local crafts and produce.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Surajpur town’s bazaars provide a friendly introduction to the district, selling everything from handloom and jaggery to forest honey, in an unhurried small-town atmosphere.

touristPlaces.name: Bhainsamundi Hidden Ghati Stretch
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A two-tier spill in the Bhainsamundi scrub, off the skywalk crowds.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Below the skywalk viewpoint crowds, Bhainsamundi’s natural spill tiers over ochre ledges into a tank of winter mist. Village women flower it at Karwa Chauth eve; the rest of the year it is a quiet soak.

touristPlaces.name: Dipadih Ruined Temple Tirth
touristPlaces.shortDesc: A village-ringed medieval temple ruin served by evening lamps.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Dipadih’s ruined temple remains a live ritual hub: villagers light lamps inside the broken sanctum every evening, carry its festival icon on Phagun carts, and guard the carved panels from vandals. Ruin and worship coexist beautifully.

touristPlaces.name: Pratappur Gond-Wood Haat
touristPlaces.shortDesc: North-haat with lac, wood-basins, and honey jars.
touristPlaces.fullDesc: Pratappur’s haat trades the forest economy — lac, carved wood-basins, honey jars and iron weather-vanes. It is food, craft and cash in one muddy fairground, far from the craft-mart gloss.
